title: Component physics defects and fidelity gaps
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md, roadmap/p3_random_findings.md, roadmap/p4_random_findings.md

Defects and fidelity gaps in the component models and the simulator core, collected while
building the RenoVisor translator (`simulation_issues.md`, 2026-07-05) and while running the
declarative migration. Fidelity items are measurable: everything the translator cannot express
shows up as `ignored`/`approximated` in its mapping report.

title: Guard the window U-value division so a TABULA row with zero window area cannot crash
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 2 ("Same division pattern for windows -- latent crash"), with the
follow-up of item 1

The window U-value is the area-weighted average `(u1*a1 + u2*a2) / (a1 + a2)`. A TABULA row with
`A_Window_1 == A_Window_2 == 0` crashes identically to the door case of item 1.

State of the code (checked 2026-09-20): item 1 is fixed --
`hisim/components/building/information.py` gives the door element
`keep_u_value_when_reference_area_is_zero=True`, and the guard skips the division when the
reference area is zero while preserving the pinned `(u * area) / area` float round trip that
shifts the last mantissa bit for 164 TABULA codes. Item 3 is fixed too
(`_thermal_bridging_conductance_in_watt_per_kelvin` uses a local value instead of writing 0.1
back into the shared dataframe). The window element declares two area columns and no such guard,
so item 2 is the one still open.

Follow-up once fixed, from item 1: `hisim/renovisor/tabula.py::_is_usable` still requires
`door > 0 and window > 0`. The `door > 0` half is already unnecessary; the `window > 0` half
becomes unnecessary with this fix, at which point the band substitution and the expectations in
`tests/renovisor/` can go back to the exact bands.

Testing: cover via a synthetic `buildingdata_ref` row with both window areas zero, and assert a
normal German code's U-value is unchanged.

title: Derive the country-specific ArcheTypeConfig defaults instead of inheriting German ones
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 14

`hisim/building_sizer_utils/interface_configs/archetype_config.py` defaults to
`weather_try_region: int = 6`, Aachen coordinates, a German postal code and a DE building code.
Non-German archetypes inherit German defaults for every field the caller does not set, and
nothing warns about the mismatch (a TRY region has no meaning for Dublin). The RenoVisor
translator overrides what it can, but any new field added with a German default silently degrades
non-DE runs.

Suggested fix: make the country-specific fields `Optional[...] = None` and derive them from
`weather_location` / `building_code` when unset; log which defaults were applied.

Testing: construct an IE archetype without the optional fields and assert no German TRY region is
used downstream.

title: Stop the DHW storage temperature running away at 3600 s timesteps
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 15 -- observed crash, listed in the document's own priority 1

Running `household_gas_building_sizer.py` (via the RenoVisor translator, config
`IE.N.SFH.04.Gen.ReEx.001.001`, full year 2019) at `seconds_per_timestep=3600` aborts with
"The water temperature in the DHW water storage is with 98.32 degC way too high or too low."
The same configuration proceeds normally at the default 900 s. The DHW charging control overshoots
when one timestep spans a whole hour (a full hour of heating power is committed before the
controller sees the new temperature): the components are stable at 15 min but not at 1 h, and
nothing validates the timestep range a setup supports.

Why it matters: coarse resolutions are the natural lever for fast batch and screening runs
(RenoVisor previews, building-sizer iterations). Today they fail late -- after component setup
and possibly hours into a batch -- rather than being either supported or rejected upfront.

Suggested fix, either or both: (1) make the DHW storage / heat-source controller timestep-aware,
scaling the hysteresis band or limiting charging power so one timestep cannot overshoot the
target band (`P_max ~ storage_capacity * dT_band / dt`); (2) have setups declare a supported
timestep range and fail fast in `SimulationParameters` validation with a clear message instead of
mid-simulation.

Testing: regression test running the gas building-sizer setup for a winter week at 900 s, 1800 s
and 3600 s, asserting the DHW temperature stays within bounds; if option 2 is chosen, assert the
clear early error instead.

title: Make the EMS restore a copy of its state rather than a reference
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states" and "Independent repairs surfaced by the
analyses" (out of scope there, named as a prerequisite for checkpointing)

`hisim/components/controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:665`:

    def i_restore_state(self) -> None:
        """Restores the state."""
        self.state = self.previous_state

That assigns the reference, not a clone, so after the first restore `self.state` and
`self.previous_state` are the same object and every later `i_save_state` and `i_restore_state`
pair is a no-op on a shared object. Siblings that get it right use `self_copy()` (see
`heat_distribution_system.py:398`).

The epic records why it matters beyond correctness in the convergence loop: `i_save_state` is a
convergence scratchpad, not a checkpoint contract, and this is one of two live bugs proving it;
both have to be fixed on their own merits before checkpoint handover (the seeded-restart tier of
the mid-year oracle) is discussable.

Done when: the restore clones, and a test forces an extra convergence iteration and asserts the
outputs are identical (the epic's M6-shaped state-leak check).

title: Make the heat-distribution controller restore its mode instead of self-assigning
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

`hisim/components/heat_distribution_system.py:1180`:

    def i_restore_state(self) -> None:
        """Restore the previous state."""
        self.controller_heat_distribution_mode = self.controller_heat_distribution_mode

The self-assignment restores nothing: whatever the controller did during a rejected convergence
iteration is kept. There is no `previous_...` attribute saved in `i_save_state` to restore from,
so the fix is to save and restore one.

The second of the two live `i_save_state` defects the mid-year analyses surfaced; both are
prerequisites for checkpoint handover.

Done when: the mode is saved and restored, and a forced extra iteration leaves the outputs
identical.

title: Split the building's initial_internal_temperature_in_celsius from the comfort floor
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states (storages, thermal mass, batteries)" and
"Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

`initial_internal_temperature_in_celsius` doubles as the permanent window-opening comfort floor
in the building's free-cooling rule -- a field named "initial" that is silently a model
parameter. The epic names it as the one blocker to untangle before any building-side seasonal
default: changing the initial temperature for a mid-year window would change the comfort rule for
the whole run.

Done when: the two meanings are separate fields, the free-cooling rule reads the comfort one, and
the goldens confirm no behaviour moved at the current values.

title: Calibrate the hplib heat pump to a stated standardized SCOP instead of the Generic fit
description:
Source: owner conversation 2026-09-21; numbers below from an EN 14825 bin-method check over the
hplib database on the same day (script not kept, method described here so it can be redone).

The RenoVisor twins heat with `MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib`, whose COP is hplib's linear curve fit
`COP = p1*T_source + p2*T_flow + p3 + p4*T_ambient` evaluated every timestep, with `model="Generic"`
(hplib's regression over its whole air/water or brine/water group). There is no way to make the
machine match a stated seasonal COP. A user knows the manufacturer's standardized SCOP (EN 14825,
average climate, at W35 or W55), so the machine should be calibrated to that figure, and the house,
climate, flow temperature and controller then produce the realized seasonal performance factor as
they do today.

Findings behind the design (2026-09-21 check):
- hplib's database carries no SCOP column, only the fit coefficients and the reference point.
- Running the EN 14825 bin method (average climate hours per outdoor-temperature bin, part load
  linear from full at -10 C to zero at 16 C, flow temperature falling from 52 C at A-7 to 30 C at
  A12 for W55 and from 34 C to 24 C for W35, inverter modulation at constant COP down to hplib's
  25 % clamp, backup rod at COP 1 above capacity) over the fit gives Generic air/water SCOP 3.40 at
  W55 and 4.74 at W35; the 366 real air/water rows span 2.95..3.65 (W55, 5th..95th percentile),
  interquartile 3.22..3.42. The device spread is narrow; realized performance is dominated by
  flow temperature and climate, which HiSim already simulates.
- Matching to the nearest database device is rejected: many devices share one SCOP with different
  temperature slopes and some fits are extrapolation artefacts (one row computes 5.57 at W55 but
  3.73 at W35, physically impossible). Calibrate the Generic fit instead.

Design:
1. Component: two optional fields on `MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig`, `standardized_scop:
   Optional[float]` and `scop_application: Optional[ScopApplication]` (Enum W35 | W55, class scope,
   no module constants). Both set or both None; one without the other is a configuration error.
2. Calibration factor k = standardized_scop / bin_scop(generic fit, application, group). COP is
   linear in its coefficients, so every COP the component takes from hplib is multiplied by k and
   the electrical power divided by k; thermal power is unchanged. hplib itself is not modified; the
   factor is applied in `get_cached_results_or_run_hplib_simulation` (or right after it) to COP and
   P_el, including the DHW branches, the heating-rod branch (cop <= 1) left as hplib returns it.
   The EER/cooling path is not scaled (out of scope, say so in the docstring).
3. The bin method lives in a small class in the component module or `hisim/components/` helper
   (e.g. `StandardisedSeasonalCop` with the bin table as a ClassVar tuple, the two flow-temperature
   lines and the sizing convention Pdesign = P_th_ref(A-7/W52) / 0.88 as named class constants with
   the source EN 14825 named in the docstring). It must be deterministic and cheap (26 bins, one
   hplib call each) and run once in `i_prepare_simulation`.
4. Ground source (group 2): same method with the brine source at 0 C in every bin and the same
   flow-temperature lines; the ambient term still uses the bin temperature.
5. Translator (`hisim/renovisor/translate.py`): when the generator is a heat pump and the request
   carries `scop` + `scop_application`, write both onto the hplib config (new `Targets` entries),
   mapping-report `used`; when only one of the two is present, refuse with a `heating.scop.*`
   problem code (fail hard, no guessing); `seasonal_efficiency_in_percent` on a heat pump house
   stays listed as not applicable. The economics context (`hisim/renovisor/economics.py`) publishes
   the SCOP as the heat pump subject's technical attribute so subsidy conditions can read it
   (remove the "No SCOP" comment block there).
6. Capability document: field probes for the two new leaves.

Tests (targeted files only, never the full suite):
- bin_scop(Generic air/water, W55) is 3.40 +- 0.05 and W35 4.74 +- 0.05 (pins the method).
- After calibration to 3.0 at W55 the bin method over the calibrated component returns 3.0 +- 0.01.
- A one-day run with standardized_scop set has P_th identical to the uncalibrated run and P_el
  scaled by 1/k in every heating timestep.
- Translator: request with both fields -> config carries them, report `used`; request with one
  field -> exit 2 with the problem code; boiler house with the percent field unchanged.
- Economics: the heat pump subject's attributes carry the SCOP.

Depends on the spec update (the maintainer's bead) because the field names and the W35/W55 enum
must be final before the translator side is written; the component side (steps 1..4) can be built
first against the config alone if the agent wants to start early.
close_reason: Done: MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig gains standardized_scop_en14825_w35/_w55; StandardizedSeasonalCop rates hplib's fit by EN 14825 (Generic air/water 3.40 at W55, 4.74 at W35); ScopCalibration solves one factor per stated rating so the calibrated fit rates exactly at them, interpolated in outlet temperature between the rating lines' heat-weighted mean outlets (28.9 / 40.7 C, decision 2026-09-23; real-data check is hisim-x2mu), applied to every heating call before caching (P_th unchanged, compressor electricity / k, rod untouched, cooling untouched). The translator writes a kept heat pump's pair onto hplib; a heating_system measure removes it with the old generator. Economics publishes nothing (physics only, renovisorissues !11), superseding design step 5's attribute.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Design update from contract PR #10 (2026-09-22): the inventory states the SCOP as a pair, heatpump_scop_en14825_w35 and heatpump_scop_en14825_w55, either may be null. Adapt design step 1: config fields standardized_scop_w35 / standardized_scop_w55 (Optional[float]) instead of standardized_scop + ScopApplication. Step 2: with both given, calibrate against both bin SCOPs (e.g. a factor per rating point, interpolated linearly in flow temperature between 35 and 55 C, held constant outside); with one given, a single factor as designed. Still blocked by hisim-epc.27 for the request-schema field names.

title: Let a caller specify battery and heat-pump sizes instead of always auto-sizing
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 5

`EnergySystemConfig` (`hisim/building_sizer_utils/interface_configs/system_config.py`) only has
`use_battery_and_ems: bool`; the battery is always auto-sized, and the heat pump is always
auto-sized from the building's heating load. RenoVisor users pick concrete sizes (battery
5/10/15 kWh, heat pump 6/8/10/12 kW) -- the translator marks these `approximated` and lets the
setup size them.

Suggested fix: add optional `battery_capacity_in_kilowatt_hours: Optional[float] = None` and
`heat_pump_thermal_power_in_kilowatt: Optional[float] = None` (None = keep auto-sizing, fully
backward compatible); in the setups, pass an explicit value through to `advanced_battery_bslib` /
`more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib` when present.

Note that under the declarative path the equivalent is a sparse `config:` override on the twin,
which the parametriser already applies -- so check whether the translator's route makes the
`EnergySystemConfig` change unnecessary before doing it.

Testing: extend the setup tests with a config carrying explicit sizes and assert the component
configs received them; keep one auto-sizing test as regression.

title: Make the heating setpoint configurable so RenoVisor's targetTempC can be mapped
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 6 (listed in the document's own priority 2, "quick wins")

Building-sizer setups hard-code `building_set_heating_temperature_in_celsius = 20.0` (and 25.0
for cooling), e.g. `household_heatpump_building_sizer.py` lines ~122-124. The user-chosen
living-room setpoint (12-28 degC in the RenoVisor UI, default 21) is ignored; every simulation
heats to 20 degC. Setpoint strongly affects heating demand (rule of thumb ~6 %/K), so this is one
of the biggest fidelity gaps for "your house today" baselines.

Suggested fix: add `set_heating_temperature_in_celsius: Optional[float] = None` to
`ArcheTypeConfig`; setups use it when present, falling back to the current constants.

Related: challenges.md C15 records that the `change room temperature` measure writes two fields
-- the building set-point and the HDS controller set-point (M11).

Testing: setup test asserting the building config receives the configured setpoint; an
integration assertion that a higher setpoint yields higher annual heating demand. Translator: map
`targetTempC` to the new field and flip its report status to `used`.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: post-MVP. new_room_temperature stays on the not-implemented whitelist and greyed out; every twin heats to the recorded 20 degC for the MVP.

title: Make boiler seasonal efficiency and design flow temperature configurable
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 9 (the document's own priority 2, "quick wins")

The gas/oil/pellet/wood setups use fixed component defaults, and `heat_distribution_system.py`
handles the flow temperature internally. RenoVisor's expert fields
`heating.seasonalEfficiencyPct` (e.g. an old oil boiler at 78 %) and `heating.flowTempC` are
dropped. Baseline fuel consumption for old boilers is therefore optimistic, which understates the
savings of switching away from them.

Suggested fix: an optional efficiency override wired to the boiler component configs; an optional
design flow temperature wired to the heat-distribution controller (also improves heat-pump COP
realism, item 5).

Testing: setup test that a lower efficiency raises annual fuel energy proportionally.

title: Add per-element U-value overrides for roof, wall and floor to the building config path
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 7; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C12, C13 and Q10

`BuildingConfig` has `window_u_value_in_watt_per_m2_per_kelvin` and `door_u_value_...` overrides
(and `hisim/components/building/information.py` honours a configured U-value per element through
`EnvelopeElement.configured_u_value_field`), but `ArcheTypeConfig` has no envelope fields and the
setups never set them. RenoVisor sends detailed envelope data (per-element construction /
insulation ids and expert U-value overrides); the translator can only express "how renovated is
it overall" via the TABULA refurbishment variant (.001/.002/.003), a three-step scale.

Suggested fix, incremental: (1) add optional per-element U-value overrides (roof, wall, floor,
window, door) to `ArcheTypeConfig` and pass them into `BuildingConfig` in the setups -- the
building component already supports window/door overrides, so extend it to roof/wall/floor;
(2) later, a derivation table (construction + insulation + added mm of material -> U-value) so
measures translate into concrete post-retrofit U-values.

Challenges Q10 settles the precedence: the inventory wins per element, TABULA otherwise, and the
report says which. C13 flags one thing to check while doing it: the floor's transmission factor
becomes a fixed 0.5 when a floor U-value is configured -- check that against a suspended floor
over a ventilated crawl space.

Testing: building-component test comparing heating demand with and without an override; setup
test that the override reaches `BuildingConfig`.
close_reason: Completed: the v2 translator writes facade, roof, floor, window and door U-values from the request into the Building config (hisim/renovisor/translate.py; tests/renovisor/test_translate.py::test_every_element_u_value_lands_on_the_building), merged as #778

title: Make ventilation and airtightness configurable (n50 and heat recovery)
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 8; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C15 (M3) and Q15

`hisim/components/building/` handles infiltration and ventilation internally; the setups only set
`enable_opening_windows = True`. RenoVisor's `air_sealing` measure (target n50 air-change rate)
and `ventilation` measure (MVHR with 75-92 % heat recovery) have no counterpart, so deep-retrofit
packages are under-represented (only via the TABULA variant bump).

Suggested fix: expose an infiltration rate (n50 or air changes per hour) on
`BuildingConfig`/`ArcheTypeConfig`, and add a mechanical-ventilation-with-heat-recovery option
(effective ventilation heat loss reduced by the recovery efficiency).

Challenges Q15 decided the three optional `BuildingConfig` fields (infiltration, shading, air
change / heat recovery) are not built for the MVP; `OUTSIDE_SHADING`,
`SHALLOW_AIR_TIGHTNESS_MEASURES`, `DIY_SEALING_OF_AIR_LEAKS` and `VENTILATION_SYSTEM` stay
`NoEffect` and are reported. This issue is the post-MVP work that closes them.

Testing: heating demand decreases monotonically with lower n50 and with higher heat-recovery
efficiency; the energy balance stays closed (`i_doublecheck`).

title: Make solar thermal an optional, sizeable flag rather than two dedicated setups
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 10

`household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py` and
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py` are the only solar-thermal setups, so an
oil- or electric-heated house with (or adding) solar thermal cannot be simulated with solar
thermal; the translator drops it with a report note. Collector area and storage volume are also
fixed by the setup rather than configurable (`solarThermal.collectorAreaM2`, `storageLiters` are
ignored).

Suggested fix: either add solar-thermal variants for the remaining heating systems or -- cleaner
long-term -- make solar thermal an optional flag handled inside each setup, with optional
collector area / storage volume fields. Under the declarative path the natural spelling is a
variant group on the recorded twins.

Related: challenges.md F10 records that the solar-thermal files wire the collector to DHW only,
so `DHW_ONLY` is the one supported supply mode; the other two catalogue values are refusals.

Testing: marker test per new combination; assert DHW energy from the boiler decreases when solar
thermal is enabled.

title: Model electric vehicles in every building-sizer setup, not only the one with a car
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 11

`household_heatpump_car_building_sizer.py` is the only building-sizer setup with a car; none of
the others model vehicles. RenoVisor models all vehicles (fuel cost and CO2 of the status quo, EV
charging load interacting with PV/battery/tariff) and the translator ignores the whole `vehicles`
array. An EV can shift several MWh/a onto the household meter, so PV/battery sizing conclusions
are skewed for EV owners.

Suggested fix: add an optional `electric_vehicles` list (annual km, kWh/km) and instantiate the
existing car / car-battery components when present, following
`household_heatpump_car_building_sizer.py`.

Blocked in part by `roadmap/p3_random_findings.md` F-9: `Car.__init__` requires
`data_dict_with_car_information` computed from the occupancy instance at setup time, so `Car`
cannot be built from configuration alone and the car setup is unrecordable (EF-33). Owner
decision 2026-08-30: leave unrecorded and name it a class-conversion gap.

Testing: setup test asserting total electricity consumption grows by about km x kWh/km; check the
EMS still converges.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-23 (from hisim-l07.12): before a RenoVisor request can run the car twin, generic_car.Car and advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery need a cost facts source (Irish device rows with sources plus adapter entries), and the owner has to decide whether the car is priced at all or treated as the household's own. tests/renovisor/test_twin_cost_declarations.py fails until then if the car twin is added to BaseFiles.

title: Represent an east-west PV split instead of approximating it as one east-facing array
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 12

`ArcheTypeConfig` has a single `pv_azimuth` and the setups build one PV array. RenoVisor offers
`east_west` roof orientation, common for terraced houses; the translator approximates it as a
single east-facing array (azimuth 90 degrees), which underestimates evening generation and
distorts self-consumption.

Suggested fix: allow a list of (azimuth, share) tuples -- or a simple `pv_split_east_west: bool`
-- and build two `PVSystem` instances with half the capacity each.

Related: challenges.md Q16 decided PV sizing reads roof form and orientation from new inventory
fields with TABULA roof geometry as the fallback, and that the rule is the existing `rooftop` law
with an added input.

Testing: compare annual generation profiles; the east/west split should flatten the midday peak
against a south array of equal kWp.

title: Decide the LCOH denominator's source so levelized_cost_of_heat stops being null on RenoVisor documents
description:
Source: ~/shared_todos/todos.md H2 (frontend, engine v20260920-1)

Observed: plan.totals.levelized_cost_of_heat_in_euro_per_kwh is null in both stage slots of the staged economics document, on every RenoVisor calculation.

Root cause: LCOH = NPV annuity / annual_heat_demand_in_kwh (calculators/aggregation.py); a missing or zero denominator omits the KPI. The denominator reaches the engine only through the declared EconomicContext (bridge _merge_context, non-negative scalars) - the simulation extract never sets it. The RenoVisor translator builds the EconomicContext BEFORE the simulation runs (run.py attaches it beside the parameters), so it cannot know the heat demand, and it states none. The engine then omits the KPI rather than dividing by an invented figure - correct per cost-spec, but the frontend wants the number.

The simulation does produce a candidate: the Building component's "Theoretical heating demand" KPI (kWh, from the TheoreticalThermalBuildingDemand channel, building.py get_kpi_entries).

Decision needed (owner):
1. Semantics: is the LCOH denominator the building-side theoretical (useful) heat demand or the generator-side delivered heat? cost-spec says "annual useful heat demand".
2. Placement: engine-side extract (bridge reads the Building KPI, declared context still overrides) benefits every run and keeps the seam promise; renovisor-side attach after the run would be two-phase and stale for re-pricing.

Done when: the denominator's source is decided, implemented, and a staged run on the mockup pair publishes a non-null LCOH in both stage slots (or the decision is "stay null" and the frontend is told so).
close_reason: Decided with Noah 2026-09-23: the LCOH divides by the useful heat the simulation measured (Building TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand + SimpleDHWStorage ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW), extracted engine-side into economic_inputs.json and annualized with simulated_period_fraction; a declared EconomicContext.annual_heat_demand_in_kwh still wins. The mockup pair publishes a non-null LCOH in both evaluations.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Answered the frontend's duplicate report renovisorissues #33 (2026-09-23): fixed on feat/lcoh-denominator, live once the next image after that PR ships.

title: Re-vendor measures.yaml after contract PR #10: material options, three new ones, the room-temperature rename
description:
Source: review of renovisor-api-contract PR #10 (`new-yamls`, commits c5d3e5f and b51a4e1, merged
2026-09-22 as ffe1304). HiSim pins `measures.yaml` and `openapi.yaml` at 5181aa5 (2026-09-17).

What changed upstream that HiSim's frozen catalogue (`hisim/renovisor/request.py` CatalogueTable)
and the translator have to follow:

1. **`material` options carry no `values` any more.** The option is declared (`name`,
   `access_level`) and its values are generated from the `materials.yaml` rows whose `measures` key
   names the measure; the values are the rows' `asp_id`s. HiSim reads the material as an object
   (`asp_id` + properties) and checks only the conductivity, so validation is unaffected, but the
   frozen table's ENUM lists ("EPS", "XPS", "EPS Foam", ...) no longer mirror the file.
2. **Three measures gained a `material` option:** `cavity_wall_insulation`,
   `basement_internal_insulation`, `top_floor_ceiling_insulation`. These are exactly the three
   `FixedMaterials.BY_MEASURE` stands in for (`hisim/renovisor/constants.py`), so the fixed table
   and its `approximated` notes go: a request names the material like for every other layer. The
   table's two ids are stale anyway (`eps_beads_cavity` -> `eps_beads`,
   `stone_wool_flexible_insulation_blankets` -> `stone_wool`).
