title: Mid-year simulation windows: start_date is ignored by every profile
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md

Mid-year simulation windows are January in disguise. Every profile-driven component indexes its
year-long profile from timestep 0 as if that were 1 January, whatever `start_date` says: weather
(all six data sources), PV, building solar gains, LPG occupancy, cars, smart devices, the CSV
loader, and the heating-season gates of the heat-pump and CHP controllers. Measured: a July week
in Aachen yields 37 kWh of PV where the true July offset yields 426 kWh (11.5x), written to disk
under a July-stamped index. The parity rig's July window is fenced pending this epic.

This epic collects the PR plan (PR1..PR8+), the window contract, the cache epoch, the split
oracle and the independent repairs the analyses surfaced.

title: Warn when the simulation year does not match the weather file's data year
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 13

`hisim/components/weather.py`'s `LocationEnum` carries NSRDB 2019 files for IE/GB/... and DWD/TRY
files for German locations; setups default to `year=2021`. The weather file's year and the
`SimulationParameters` year are independent, so simulating year X with weather of year Y silently
misaligns weekdays and (for leap years) day counts. The RenoVisor translator hard-codes 2019 for
this reason, but nothing in HiSim checks or documents the constraint.

Suggested fix: `Weather.i_prepare_simulation` should log a warning (or raise, behind a flag) when
the requested simulation year does not match the data year of the selected weather file; expose
the data year on `LocationEnum` entries instead of parsing it from filenames.

This sits next to the mid-year window epic: the same "which calendar does this profile speak"
question, from the year side rather than the offset side. The epic's leap-year refusal (PR2) is
the decidable half.

Testing: unit test that a mismatched year triggers the warning; no behaviour change otherwise.

title: Give generic_price_signal a time-varying profile instead of element [0] forever
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses" -- out of
scope for the epic, with its trigger named

`generic_price_signal` emits a constant: it reads element `[0]` of its profile forever. It is not
profile-driven in the epic's sense, so it cannot be made wrong by the mid-year work. The trigger
for fixing it: when a setup needs a time-varying tariff.

Note that `generic_price_signal` moved to `obsolete/components/` under P4 decision D-16
(2026-09-10), and that `TariffProvider` is the live component that publishes per-timestep prices
(cost_module_issues.md 17). So this may be moot; confirm before acting.

title: Explain the uninterpretable 10/15 Wh literal in the MPC controller
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses" -- out of
scope, "flag for whoever touches the MPC"

The MPC carries an uninterpretable `10/15` Wh literal. Whoever next touches the MPC should find
out what it means and name it, or delete it.

Note that `controller_mpc` moved to `obsolete/components/` under P4 decision D-16 (2026-09-10),
so this may only matter if the MPC comes back. The Rust feasibility review's Tier 4 question
("MPC and casadi: reformulate as a MILP, accept a permanent Python island, or declare MPC out of
core scope") is the larger decision above it.

title: Settle the contradictory initial-state defaults for storages, the EV and hydrogen
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states (storages, thermal mass, batteries)" and
"Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses" (out of scope there, trigger: when the
season-aware storage seed lands)

Measured contradictions recorded by the analyses: the buffer storage starts at a hard-coded
35 degC while its dataclass default is 25 degC; the EV state of charge is 0 in one place and 0.5
in another; the hydrogen storage is 80 % full in one package and empty in the other -- arbitrary
twice over. DHW storage at 60 degC is season-neutral and correct; battery SOC 0 settles in a PV
day; about 25 controllers start "off" with their minimum idle time blocking the first 15-60
minutes, which is a season-neutral start artefact.

The epic's decision: keep the defaults and document the measured per-component transient, plus
exactly one season-aware change -- the buffer / space-heating storage seeds from the
heating-season gate, so outside the season it starts at ambient 20 degC instead of 35 degC (a
buffer nobody has charged sits at room temperature, the one derivation defensible in a sentence).
Warm-up prefixes are rejected on the measured evidence.

Done when: each component's initial value has one definition, the contradictions are gone, and
the season-aware buffer seed lands with its goldens.

title: PR1: one window contract, YEARLYFORECAST renames and the dead smart device deleted
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR1, "The window contract (one chokepoint)"
and "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

First PR of the mid-year epic: establish the single window chokepoint, rename the
`YEARLYFORECAST`-shaped names to window names, fix the plot labels, and delete the dead
`generic_smart_device` (zero references, raises `KeyError` on first call -- deleting it also
retires the independently broken `convert_lpg_timestep_to_utc` and the test that pins its wrong
output).

Blast-radius rule for the whole epic: PR2 and PR4+5 must not move a single January golden (offset
0 on 1 January is each PR's own cheapest proof).

Done when: there is exactly one place that decides a run's window, and the renames and deletion
are in with no golden movement.

title: PR2: an offset primitive the weather adopts, plus the leap refusal and the four anchors
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR2, "The design: B' -- the profile owner
resolves one offset against its own frame", "Caches: the epoch" and "Independent repairs"

The offset primitive plus the weather adopting it; the leap-year refusal (the offset lookup is
where "this source cannot serve this date" is decidable); the DWD_15MIN reader, which sizes its
index from the run's duration instead of the file and is the one reader that cannot be sliced
until anchored; deleting the dead building solar-gain cache (delete, do not fix the `hasattr`
typo -- repairing it would serve stale entries past every check and add a sixth window-sensitive
cache); the four unit anchors; and building the oracle harness. Bumps the cache epoch.

The four unit anchors, in `tests/`: first-timestep identity against the source's own labels; the
DST phase pins (260 550 / 260 610 / 260 640 and a December mirror); each weather reader's
`index[0]` pinned (the six sources use three different anchors -- Berlin 00:30, Berlin 00:00
after the padding row `Weather.interpolate` prepends, and UTC 00:00, which is exactly why
"resolve against the delivered frame" is the rule); and the cold-then-warm cache equality
assertion.

The harness is `scripts/midyear_oracle.py`, modelled on the parity rig (per-run empty cache
directory, one process, one printed verdict table, a tolerance flag that shouts when nonzero),
reusing `ResultComparison` verbatim -- its index check refuses a misaligned slice for free.

Done when: PR2 moves no January golden and the oracle runs.

title: PR3: rewrite convert_lpg_data_to_utc as localize, convert, slice
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR3

`convert_lpg_data_to_utc` is rewritten as localize -> convert -> slice. This changes January
numbers too: the current code starts every window at source row 60 and fabricates the final hour.
It is therefore the deliberate January re-bless of the epic and ships alone, so the golden diff
has exactly one cause. Bumps the cache epoch.

Depends on PR2 (the offset primitive).

Done when: the conversion is date-correct, the January goldens are re-blessed in one commit whose
message names this as the single cause, and nothing else is in the PR.

title: PR4+5: the LPG connector owns occupancy and cars in all three modes, gates go day-of-year
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR4+5 -- MUST SHIP TOGETHER

The LPG connector owns the window offset for occupancy and for the cars, in all three data
acquisition modes, and the seasonal gates (the heat-pump and CHP controllers' heating-season
checks) go day-of-year. These must ship together, or a July window heats the house. Bumps the
cache epoch.

Depends on PR3.

Blast-radius rule: must not move a single January golden -- offset 0 on 1 January is the PR's own
cheapest proof.

title: PR6: the solar thermal collector consumes the weather's window instead of its own sun
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR6 and "Independent repairs surfaced by
the analyses"

The solar-thermal collector drops its naive-UTC duplicate sun position and consumes the weather's
published window. This is one of the two places that honour the date today, which is what makes a
mid-year run incoherent rather than correct -- the collector sees a genuine July sun (apparent
zenith 27.7 degrees) wired to January irradiance. Three solar-thermal goldens move. Bumps the
cache epoch.

Depends on PR2.

Done when: there is one sun position per run, and the three goldens are re-blessed.

title: PR7: lift the July fence in its five sites and bless the first true July goldens
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR7; the fence is recorded in
`scripts/p3_parity_matrix.py` and R11.5 as amended 2026-09-06

Lift the fence in its five sites -- the parity workflow's hand-kept window options among them,
which nothing derives from the code -- invert the fence test into "July differs from January",
add the `july_week` parameter set to `scripts/golden_config.json` and bless the first true July
references.

This is what unfences the parity rig's July window, which P6 of the declarative plan needs to
confirm the stack green "over every runnable window".

Depends on PR4+5 and PR6.

title: PR8+: every stateful component expresses its complete state as startup configuration
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR8+ and "Validation: the split oracle"

A series, one component per PR. Run the full year once, read every stateful component's state at
the window start (the battery's SOC on 1 July, the storage temperatures, the thermal-mass
temperature, the controllers' modes and timers), hand those to the window run as startup values,
and the whole comparison becomes an exact gate: with its complete mid-cycle state handed over,
even a bang-bang controller continues on the very limit cycle the year run was on, so the one
column no warm-up could ever buy back (`WaterMassFlowHDS`, permanently 16.7 % out) joins the gate
too.

What it costs is completeness -- a partially seeded component just re-imports its transient --
and not every component can express its state as configuration today (controller idle timers, the
meters' cumulative sums, the EMS's internals are not config fields). So the seeded tier grows
component by component: a column moves from the oracle's report tier to the exact gate the moment
its component's full state is expressible as startup configuration. The cumulative meter columns
move immediately, gated on first differences instead of levels.

This is checkpoint handover at the configuration level, which is why it shares its prerequisites
with the two `i_save_state` repairs (the EMS reference restore and the HDS self-assignment).

The series moves no golden at all: startup values default to today's constants, and each PR's
proof is its component's columns going exactly to zero in the seeded oracle.

Depends on PR7.

title: Rust conversion ideas
Profile a representative run and publish the time breakdown
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Step 0 -- "Measure before
changing anything"

Two or three setups (one minutely full year, one 15-minute short run, one with MPC), broken into:
timestep loop, third-party library calls (pvlib/hplib/bslib/windpowerlib), input parsing,
postprocessing, external waiting (UTSP/LPG). This is a day of work and it is the gate on every
performance argument in the companion feasibility document -- including whether Tier 1 should be
reordered around whatever actually dominates.

Payoff now: it will almost certainly find optimizable Python nobody has looked at.
Payoff for a port: it converts "10-50x on the loop" into an Amdahl ceiling for the whole run.

title: Stop the byte surgery that appends to component_connections.json
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2

`component.py:447` seeks to `st_size - 1` and overwrites the closing bracket of
`component_connections.json` to append an entry. Buffer the connections and write the file once
when wiring completes.

Payoff now: an interrupted run stops leaving a syntactically broken JSON file behind.

title: Make the convergence criterion explicit, configurable and unit-aware
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2; and
roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md option O8, "Per-output tolerance vector"

`component.py:194` compares every output against a hardcoded absolute 1e-4 -- watts, joules,
kelvin, euros and dimensionless ratios on one scale -- and the forced-convergence thresholds
(above 10 iterations forced, above 100 raises, `simulator.py:266-270`) are hardcoded next to it.
At minimum make all three configurable and document the choice; ideally scale per unit.

O8 states the targeted form: replace the single absolute 1e-4 with a per-output (or per-unit)
tolerance supplied at construction. It is the cheap fix for the real defect measurement M4 looks
for -- an absolute threshold applied across incommensurable units, where a counter at 1e9 needs
1e-13 relative and would fail on every iteration, silently forcing the 10-iteration cutoff on
every timestep.

Caution from O8: it changes iteration counts and therefore results. Needs a one-time golden
re-bless and a stated policy, per the parity-policy decision.

Payoff now: the tolerance becomes a modelling decision that can be justified, and the "runs
converge but nobody knows how tightly" question gets an answer.

Gated on measurement M4.

title: Give i_save_state and i_restore_state explicit state structs instead of deepcopy
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

Five component modules `deepcopy` themselves or their state each iteration. An explicit small
state object is faster in Python and removes the "which attributes are state?" ambiguity.

Payoff now: measurable -- this runs once per component per convergence iteration per timestep.

Related: the two live `i_save_state` defects (the EMS restoring a reference and the
heat-distribution controller self-assigning) are exactly the ambiguity this removes, and the
mid-year epic names both as prerequisites for checkpoint handover.

title: Inject the cache backend, the clock and the RNG instead of monkeypatching them in tests
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

22 test files use `monkeypatch`, 8 of them around `utils.get_cache_file`; without that patching,
runs are order-dependent through the shared on-disk cache, and `conftest.py` scrubs
`HISIM_CACHE_*` around every test. Turn these into constructor parameters.

Payoff now: order-independent tests, less autouse machinery, and the stale-cache class of false
failures loses its main route in.

This also matches the AGENTS.md guideline that monkeypatching is to be avoided in shared
fixtures, and the seeded-RNG precedent of `RandomNumbers`, whose seed became a configuration
field in P3 so a system description can say what a run will do.

title: Write an owned, versioned cache-key serializer with a stable field order
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

The cache key is `sha256(dataclasses_json output + sim-params string)`, so field order, float repr
and enum spelling from a third-party library are load-bearing for about 319 MB of committed cache
and every cross-machine share. Write an owned key serializer with a stable field order, a schema
version in the key, and a test that pins the exact string for a fixture config.

Payoff now: upgrading `dataclasses_json` or `pyhumps` stops silently invalidating every cache
entry in the fleet.

Related: the producer-fingerprint keys of the cache service solve the other half (what code
produced the content); this one is about what identifies the request.

title: Audit the sixty exact float comparisons in component control flow
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

Roughly 60 `== 0`-style comparisons sit in component control paths
(`water_mass_flow_rate == 0`, `control_signal == 0.0`, `delta_t == 0` patched to `1e-8`).
Replace with documented epsilons and re-bless the goldens once.

Do this in Python, where re-blessing is cheap and reviewable, rather than discovering it during a
port where the change is indistinguishable from a translation bug.

title: Move module_selection.py out of hisim/inputs and stop reading data at import time
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

`hisim/inputs/photovoltaic/module_selection.py` is Python inside `hisim/inputs/`, and it reads PV
module databases at import. Relocate to `hisim/components/` and make the read lazy.

Payoff now: import time, and the data directory becomes purely data.

title: Prune requirements.txt of the three declared but unimported packages
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

`seaborn`, `plotly` and `html2image` are declared but imported nowhere under `hisim/`, `tests/`,
`tools/`, `scripts/` or `system_setups/`; there are commented-out pins (`pvlib`,
`windpowerlib`, `wetterdienst`) and a migration TODO.

An accurate dependency list is a prerequisite for reasoning about the domain-library gap at all,
and the commented-out pvlib pin is named separately in the Tier 1 adapter item as a risk of its
own.

Note that `pyhumps` already left with the scenario-JSON writer (P4 F-9), so the list has drifted
since the survey.

title: Converge on the energy-system YAML as the only way to describe a system
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3, "Converge on one
front end"

At the time of the survey there were three ways to describe a system: 23 setup functions in
`system_setups/*.py`, 22 `.scenario.json` twins and 28 `.energy_system.yaml` files, with
byte-identity freshness gates keeping the generated ones in sync. Per the declarative-energy-
systems plan the YAML is the intended survivor; finish that migration and retire the others.

The JSON third retired on 2026-09-12, so what is left is retiring the Python setups, which is
P5/P6 work in the declarative plan.

Payoff now: one loader to keep correct instead of three, and one place where a new component must
be registered.
Payoff for a port: the single largest reduction in porting surface available anywhere in this
list.

title: Decide what happens to MPC and casadi before any port is estimated
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4 -- "Decisions to take
before a port, not cleanups"

Reformulate MPC as a MILP (the feasibility document argues the dynamics are linear between
disjunctions), accept a permanent Python island, or declare MPC out of core scope.

This is the only red item in the whole analysis; leaving it open leaves the total open.

Note that `controller_mpc` moved to `obsolete/components/` under P4 decision D-16 (2026-09-10),
which is close to "out of core scope" already but was not taken as this decision.

title: Give every physics library one HiSim-owned adapter module with no library types in signatures
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

Today `pvlib`, `hplib`, `bslib`, `windpowerlib`, `oemof.thermal` and `pygfunction` are called
inline from the components that need them -- `weather.py`, `generic_pv_system.py`,
`building/window.py`, `solar_thermal_system.py`, `more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py`,
`simple_heat_source.py` -- and library objects cross the boundary in both directions (HiSim
mutates `heatpump.delta_t` on an hplib object mid-simulation). Give each library one HiSim-owned
module with typed scalar/array inputs and outputs and no library type in its signatures.

Payoff now: upgrading or pinning pvlib stops being a repo-wide risk (the pin in
`requirements.txt` is commented out, which is its own finding); the calls become mockable, so
component tests stop needing real solar-position math; and one place can record reference
inputs and outputs per library call.
Payoff for a port: this boundary is the FFI seam, and it is the difference between a hybrid being
designable and not.

title: Decide whether charts and the PDF report are in core scope
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4

Docker mode already runs with every chart and the PDF disabled, which proves they are optional.
Decide whether they are in core scope; if not, formalize the JSON manifest that external tooling
would render.

(The container post-processing allow-list that made "Docker mode" a different option set was
removed on 2026-09-19 with HiSim #780 -- the simulation file is authoritative in a container too
-- so the evidence the item leans on is historical. The decision stands.)

title: Decide whether the core simulator may depend on the closed-source .NET LPG binary
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4

The forever-dependency is the closed-source .NET binary, not the Python wrapper. Decide whether
the core simulator may depend on a subprocess at all.

The operational evidence for how much that dependency costs is in
`roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md`: the shared sqlite database that was never found, the
whole-calculation lock that serialises local runs, and the ETXTBSY install race.

title: Decide the FFI direction before estimating a hybrid
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 4 -- "the FFI direction
(review item R5)", one of "two decisions masquerading as engineering tasks"

Does Python call into Rust (an extension module inside the existing run) or does Rust drive and
call back into Python for the components not yet ported? The feasibility document's review item
R5 sets out the trade; `rust_simulator_spec.md` option O7 sketches the Rust
`process_one_timestep` under the second reading, including the mechanics that will bite (hold the
GIL across the timestep rather than re-acquiring per call; call `Python::check_signals()` once
per timestep or Ctrl-C stops working on long runs; decide how a `PyErr` from a component becomes
a Rust error and back with the traceback intact, including the existing raise at 100 iterations).

Gated on measurements M2 and M3.

title: M0: measure per-element container read and write costs on our CPython
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2 "Measurement program", M0

Read and write cost for `list`, `array.array('d')`, `memoryview` format `'d'`, and numpy scalar
indexing. Establishes where the boxing conversion is cheapest to pay.

Expected ordering, to be confirmed and not assumed: list fastest per element, every unboxed
buffer slower, numpy slowest -- which is why an unboxed buffer handed to Python is the wrong
shape. A prior team measurement already found converting the value store to numpy came out
slower: the vectorized compare gain is smaller than the loss on hundreds of individual scalar
stores.

title: M1: measure the four i_simulate call-site spellings on one representative component
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M1

One representative component, four `i_simulate` bodies: (a) the current
`stsv.set_output_value(self.channel, v)`; (b) `o[self.channel.local_index] = v`;
(c) `o[self.IDX_X] = v` with a class-level int; (d) `o[2] = v` with the index hoisted to a local.

Decides whether rewriting 717 call sites (484 `set_output_value` and 233 `get_input_value` under
`hisim/components/`) earns its churn, and which spelling to rewrite them to. It is also the gate
on options O3, O5 and O6 of the same document -- in particular whether the gap between spellings
(b)/(c) and (d) is worth a port-plumbing generator.

title: M2: measure the PyO3 boundary cost with a gather-and-scatter stub
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M2 -- the only measurement that
needs a Rust toolchain

One extension call that gathers 10 scattered f64 into a Python list and scatters 7 back. Yields
the real crossing cost and the real per-float boxing cost on our platform, which every estimate
in the options register depends on. It is also the cheapest available probe of the Rust build and
wheel story.

title: M3: split per-iteration time into component physics versus value plumbing
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M3

Per-iteration time split into component physics versus value plumbing (writes, reads, the
compare, and the copies), on two or three representative setups. Without this, every speedup
figure in the options register is unanchored.

The plumbing it measures: per iteration the engine does one full-array `copy_values_from_other`
(`component.py:171-179`) and two `clone()` per timestep (`simulator.py:239-241`), plus an
interpreted loop over every output at absolute 1e-4 (`component.py:191-197`).

title: M4: log which output fails the convergence test last, per timestep
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M4 -- "residual argmax"

Per timestep, log which output index fails `is_close_enough_to_previous` last. This answers two
questions at once: whether the outputs driving the iteration count are wired signals or
write-only diagnostics (on the measured 14-component setup, 141 outputs are registered and only
41 distinct ones are read, so about 71 % of outputs are read by no component), and whether any
output's magnitude makes the absolute 1e-4 threshold unsatisfiable -- a counter at 1e9 needs
about 1e-13 relative, so it would fail on every iteration and silently force the 10-iteration
cutoff on every timestep.

This is the gate on the per-output tolerance vector.

title: M5: measure the iteration histogram and the result-buffer memory high-water
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M5

The distribution of iterations per timestep, and the peak size of `all_result_lines`. A year at
1 min x 141 outputs is about 593 MB as raw f64 but roughly 2-3 GB as a Python list of lists of
boxed floats; at 500 outputs it is about 2 GB versus about 10 GB. Given the 16 GB runner ceiling
tracked by `ci-usage`, this may be worth more than any CPU figure in the register.

title: M6: assert that one forced extra convergence iteration leaves the outputs identical
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md, section 2, M6 -- "state-leak test
(correctness, not performance)"

Run a timestep, then force one extra iteration, and assert the outputs are identical. This checks
the premise that `i_restore_state` undoes everything `i_simulate` mutates. If it fails anywhere,
the loop is not a fixed-point iteration, iteration count changes results, and several arguments
in the options register and Appendix A do not hold.

Worth having regardless of the whole Rust programme -- which is why it is P3 among P4 siblings.

It will fail on at least two components today: the EMS restores a reference rather than a clone
(`controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:665`) and the heat-distribution controller
self-assigns (`heat_distribution_system.py:1180`). Both have their own issues.

title: Replace the string-keyed SimRepository with a typed simulation context
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

17 modules under `hisim/` still reach for the singleton, including the weather -> building
forecast handoff (11 yearly arrays), price signal -> MPC (about 20 forecast keys), the
air-conditioner fit coefficients and the PID thermal coefficients; `generic_car.py:293` reads its
repository through `getattr(self, "simulation_repository", None)`. Replace with an explicit typed
context constructed by the engine and passed to components.

(Counts are from the 2026-09-09 survey at f91c3eb1. `hisim/sim_repository_singleton.py` was
deleted on 2026-09-12 and the weather and occupancy forecasts moved into the per-simulation
`SimRepository` under writer-owned key names, so the singleton half is smaller than the survey
says; the string-keyed half is what remains.)

Payoff now: mypy sees these handoffs, a missing publisher fails at wiring time instead of as a
`KeyError` in timestep 0, test fixtures that reset a global disappear, and run isolation stops
depending on discipline.
Payoff for a port: removes the single largest piece of untyped shared mutable state.

title: Replace pd.DataFrame in the component cost and KPI hooks with a typed results view
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

92 signatures under `hisim/components/` take `postprocessing_results: pd.DataFrame`, so pandas is
part of the component API and every cost/KPI implementation depends on column-name conventions.
Introduce a narrow view type (a per-output series accessor plus the reductions actually used) and
migrate the hooks behind it.

Payoff now: KPI and cost code becomes unit-testable without constructing a DataFrame; the
column-name coupling that section 6.2 of the feasibility document describes as "positional
column-name parsing" becomes a compile-time-visible interface.
Payoff for a port: removes pandas from the component trait, which is otherwise a hard blocker for
porting any component before porting all of postprocessing.

title: Replace reflection-based component instantiation with a static registry
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 1

29 `importlib` call sites across 9 component modules exist purely to dodge circular imports in
default connections, and the energy-system YAML files name components by fully-qualified Python
path (`class: hisim.components.weather.Weather`). Add a name -> constructor table with a test that
pins its contents, keep the fully-qualified paths accepted as aliases, and let the declarative
loaders resolve through the table.

(The survey counted 22 `.scenario.json` files too; those were retired on 2026-09-12, so the 28
`.energy_system.yaml` files are the live half.)

Payoff now: a typo in a file fails at load with a suggestion instead of an `ImportError` from
deep inside `importlib`; the circular-import dodges can be deleted; the component inventory
becomes enumerable for docs, the webtool and `hisim energy-system describe`.
Payoff for a port: this is the inventory Rust cannot generate for itself, and building it in
Python proves the list is complete.

Related: this is also the fix for the two `Building` class spellings in the v3 schema.

title: Decide the numeric-parity policy and make the goldens implement it
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2 (first item) and
Tier 4 ("the parity policy ... a decision masquerading as an engineering task")

Today the regression corpus mixes byte comparison of CSV and markdown with `math.isclose` at
`rel_tol` 1e-9 and `pytest.approx` at its implicit 1e-6 default. Byte comparison pins pandas'
float formatting, which is why pandas is pinned to an exact version. Move comparisons to parsed-
value numeric comparison at declared per-domain tolerances, and keep byte identity only where
byte identity is the point (the `.energy_system.yaml` freshness gates).

Payoff now: goldens stop breaking on formatting changes in a dependency, and every tolerance
becomes a stated decision rather than a library default nobody chose.
Payoff for a port: this is the acceptance harness; review item R6 in the feasibility document
explains why the current contradiction blocks the estimate itself.

The document's explicit non-recommendation belongs with it: do not chase bit-exactness. It is
unattainable across languages and it also means faithfully reproducing known defects.

Related: the golden gate's `abs_tol = 0` floor, which makes a physically zero KPI incomparable,
is the first concrete instance.

title: Pass the OPEX cost values in memory instead of re-reading the CSVs it wrote
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2, "Kill the intra-run
file feedback loop in postprocessing"

KPI preparation re-reads the cost CSVs that the OPEX step wrote earlier in the same run, keyed by
magic row names such as "Total" (`kpi_preparation.py:732-776`). Pass the values in memory.

Payoff now: removes an ordering dependency between postprocessing options and a whole class of
"works alone, fails in the full run" bugs.

Related: cost_module_issues.md item 27 records a second ordering hazard in the same area -- the
legacy `get_cost_capex` writes computed values back into component configs, which the lifecycle
engine then read as overrides until the engine was moved to run first.

title: Replace the pickle result export with parquet or CSV plus JSON
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2

`postprocessing_main.py` pickles a DataFrame. Pickle has no cross-language reader and is a
security and version-compatibility liability in Python too.

This one has external consumers, so it needs an announcement and a deprecation window -- start it
early precisely because of that.

title: Split physics from cost and reporting boilerplate in the large component modules
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2

Section 4.1 of the feasibility document estimates that 25-40 % of the big component files is
cost, KPI and report code. Split per component, one PR each, no behaviour change.

Payoff now: `building.py` at 2 099 lines and `more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py` at about 2 750
become reviewable, and the physics gets testable without the reporting stack.

(The building has since been split into a package, `hisim/components/building/` -- so it is an
example of the shape rather than a remaining case.)

title: Declarative energy systems (P4 sweep, twins, recording)
Give KPI keys stable addresses so consumers stop rebuilding key strings by hand
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_cleanup_todos.md, "Missing deliverables (code)"; spec
`roadmap/kpi_address_spec.md`

KPI keys are still volatile -- bare unless a collision exists -- and consumers rebuild key
strings by hand. The spec `roadmap/kpi_address_spec.md` is on main and describes the fix; its own
step 6 is "remove the volatile keys remark from `roadmap/p3_cleanup_todos.md` once merged".

Why it matters beyond tidiness, from the Rust survey (Tier 2, "Retire the magic-string KPI
keys"): about 100 KPI names are matched by string equality across files, with a building-sizer
lookup matching whole sentences, so a renamed KPI silently zeroes a downstream number instead of
failing. That item says explicitly to align with this spec rather than fork a second scheme.

Related: `roadmap/p3_random_findings.md` F-28 -- the EMS builds
`KpiEntry(name=f"Priority for {input_sorted.field_name}")`, so an aggregator port name is
embedded in a KPI key, which is a second argument for renaming the legacy aggregator ports.

Done when: keys are addressable and stable, and no consumer builds one by string concatenation.

title: Give the parity rig a verdict that distinguishes an unrunnable environment from a disagreement
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-15 (reported, 2026-09-15)

`scripts/p3_parity_check.py` gives each of its two sides a private, empty cache directory and
deletes the whole work directory at the start of every triple (`p3_parity_check.py:159`,
`p3_parity_runs.py:324`), which is right for the question it asks: a shared cache would let one
side answer from the other side's result. The consequence is that every setup whose occupancy
comes from `USE_LOCAL_LPG` must actually run the LoadProfileGenerator binary, twice, on every
invocation. On a machine where that binary fails -- here the root filesystem was 98 % full and
the binary died with `System.IO.IOException: No space left on device`, leaving no results and no
log -- no such setup can be measured, and the rig reports a parity failure rather than an
unrunnable environment: three identical FAIL rows whose note is "the python run did not finish".
The golden gate has no such problem, since it uses the normal cache directory and a seeded entry
answers both modes.

Two things would help, neither a change to the isolation the rig needs: a verdict that
distinguishes "the run could not start" from "the two sides disagree" (the note already carries
the distinction, the verdict does not), and an opt-in read-only seed directory the private caches
are pre-filled from, so a profile that is an input to both sides rather than a result of either
can be supplied once.

title: Retire PVSystemConfig.location, a string nobody reads, with the PV conversion
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-7 (verified; logged 2026-09-03, re-verified 2026-09-12
against main)

`PVSystemConfig.location: str` (`hisim/components/generic_pv_system.py:116`) is passed by 23
setup call sites (`location=weather_location`) and written into all 27 PV blocks of the committed
energy-system YAMLs, and the PV component never reads it: inside the module it appears seven
times -- the module docstring, the dataclass field, a parameter of the two factory methods and
their two forwardings, and one docstring line -- and in no computation.

Its purpose was to make the PV cache key differ between sites, which worked only as long as every
setup copied the same variable into the weather and the PV -- a habit, not an invariant, and the
origin of `pylpg_flakiness.md` F7. F7 has since landed: the PV carries a `weather_identity` field
sized from the weather itself (`generic_pv_system.py:145`), so the key no longer needs `location`.
What remains is a field that can visibly disagree with its neighbour: a setup with Seville
weather and a PV built with the factories' default `location="Aachen"` records
`location: Aachen` beside `weather_identity: Sevilla/...`, and the first is wrong without
consequence.

The finding's own instruction: do not fix piecemeal. The field is in the config class, two
factory signatures, 23 setup call sites, one test and 27 energy-system YAML blocks, and the
conversion of `PVSystemConfig` is the point at which those are all rewritten anyway.

title: Move the car battery's charged and discharged totals off its configuration
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-20 (reported, 2026-09-16, left alone in batch B7)

Two fields of `CarBatteryConfig`, `total_charged_energy_in_kilowatthour` and
`total_discharged_energy_in_kilowatthour`, are not inputs at all: `CarBattery.get_cost_opex` and
`CarBattery.get_component_kpi_entries` each compute them from the post-processing results and
assign them back onto `self.battery_config`, so the configuration object a run started with is a
different object by the time the run ends. They carry a 0.0 default and the twin records them as
0.0, which is true of the configuration as written and untrue of the configuration as it ends up.

That a configuration is the author's statement of the system, read and never written, is what
lets the recorder diff a live config against a built preset and call the difference an override.
Here the difference is a result. Nothing is wrong today only because the two writes happen in
post-processing, after the last recording; a recorder that ran later, or a second post-processing
pass, would write two computed energies into a file as if an author had typed them.

Two honest ways out, per the finding. Move the accumulators onto the component -- they are
per-run state, which is what a component holds -- and let the two methods read and write
`self.total_charged_energy...`; the config loses two fields and the twin two lines. Or keep them
where they are and exclude them from recording, which needs a way to mark a field as
not-an-input that the recorder, `describe` and the schema all honour, and which would be the
first such mark in the repository. The first is smaller and says the true thing; it changes the
component's behaviour surface and the twin, which is why B7 (a behaviour-neutral batch) left it.

title: Decide what to do with the run-side description that nothing reads
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-24 (reported, 2026-09-18, found while retiring the
scenario JSON)

A run's one-line description travels a long way: the Python entry point takes it from the first
line of the setup file, a declarative run takes it from the energy-system file's `description`
field, `Simulator.description` carries it, `PostProcessingDataTransfer` carries it -- and its
single consumer was the `description` field of `scenario.json`, which no longer exists. Nothing
reads it now.

The description of the file is not in question: it documents the system for whoever opens the
file, the recorder writes it and the loader reads it back. What has no reader is the copy the run
object carries.

Three honest ways out: drop the run-side chain and leave the field to the file (smallest, and it
takes `hisim_main`'s docstring-scraping block with it); give it a consumer, the obvious one being
the PDF report, which today prints no description of the run it reports on; or leave it and say
so, which is what the entry does for now.

The scenario name is in a similar position but not the same one: its one remaining consumer, the
`scenario` column of the pyam export, is live -- see the pyam retirement question.

title: Decide whether the pyam scenario-evaluation export is still needed
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-25 (reported, 2026-09-18; logged rather than done on the
owner's instruction)

`pyam` is not a dependency and is imported nowhere. What exists is
`PREPARE_OUTPUTS_FOR_SCENARIO_EVALUATION`, which writes the run's results resampled to four
resolutions -- `hourly/daily/monthly/yearly_<n>_days.csv` in
`result_data_for_scenario_evaluation/` -- in the pyam long format, one row per variable carrying
`model, scenario, region, variable, unit, year, value`.

Its reader is already gone. `hisim/postprocessing/scenario_evaluation/` --
`result_data_collection.py`, `result_data_processing.py`, `result_data_plotting.py` and
`scenario_analysis_complete_with_config.py`, the tool that read those CSVs back and compared runs
-- was moved to `obsolete/` in #541 (2026-08-10) and left the repository entirely with the rest
of that tree in #590. The writer stayed. `hisim/postprocessing/__init__.py` still tells a reader
that results "can be compared and visualised with the `hisim.postprocessing.scenario_evaluation`
sub-package", which has not existed for six weeks.

Nothing else in the tree reads the CSVs: the building sizer reads `all_kpis.json` and
`*_kpi_config_for_building_sizer.json`, and neither RenoVisor nor the HPC harness touches the
directory. What is not known is whether anyone reads them outside the repository -- unlike the
scenario JSON, this artifact carries results rather than configuration, and the pyam long format
is the interchange format for cross-run comparison, so an analysis workflow living elsewhere is
plausible. That question is the whole of the decision, and it is the owner's.

What retiring it would take with it, about 300 lines and the last of the run metadata:
`prepare_results_for_scenario_evaluation` and its four helpers with the four
`self.model/scenario/region/year` attributes; `region_of`, whose only caller it is, and
`tests/test_postprocessing_region.py` entirely; the option in eleven building-sizer setups, three
legacy `*.simulation.json` parameter files and five test files. And the scenario name: the
`scenario` column of this export is its one remaining consumer since F-9, so
`Simulator.scenario_name`, the building sizers' hash strings, `EnergySystemFile.name` as a run
name and `scenario_name_of` for grouped runs would all become decoration. With F-24's description
that is the entire run-metadata layer.

At minimum, correct the stale pointer in `hisim/postprocessing/__init__.py` either way.

title: Repair or delete 2021_minutely_full.simulation.json, which names two dead options
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-26 (verified, 2026-09-18; left broken deliberately)

`system_setups/2021_minutely_full.simulation.json` -- the repository's only "full" parameter set,
the one a reader reaches for when they want everything -- lists `MAKE_RESULT_JSON_FOR_WEBTOOL`
and `MAKE_OPERATION_RESULTS_FOR_WEBTOOL` among its options. Both left `PostProcessingOptions` on
2026-06-26 (88869070, "more old webtool cleanup"). The Python entry point resolves option names
with `PostProcessingOptions[option]` (`hisim_main.py:148`), so loading that file raises a bare
`KeyError` naming the string, wherever it is loaded rather than where it is wrong. The
declarative reader refuses an unknown name properly, by name and location; the JSON path does
not.

The other six `system_setups/*.simulation.json` load cleanly, checked the same way. Nothing in
the repository references the broken one, which is why nothing noticed.

Left broken deliberately: it belongs to the imperative JSON parameter path, which retires with
the Python setups in P5/P6, and repairing it now would suggest the file is maintained. The YAML
library that replaces it holds every file to the rule this one broke: a test loads each one and
refuses an option name the enum does not have.

Two ways to close it: delete the file when the Python path goes, or -- if someone wants it before
then -- drop the two dead names, which makes it the one JSON parameter set with a live full
option list.

title: Settle what my_sim.my_module_config is allowed to hold across the eleven sizers
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox

Nine sizers mutate `my_sim.my_module_config` to a dict on the fallback path; the two heat-pump
sizers do not, so downstream readers see a different type depending on the sibling. One behaviour
for all eleven.

`read_in_configs` is string-only by decision (review round of 2026-09-06: it refuses a non-string
with a `TypeError`), so this repair has to settle what the attribute is allowed to hold rather
than widening the reader to accept both.

Done when: the eleven sizers agree, the allowed type is stated, and a test pins it.

title: Make the four sizers that ignore weather_filepath and weather_datasource read or refuse them
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox

Four sizers ignore `weather_filepath` / `weather_datasource`:
`household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer`, `household_heatpump_car_building_sizer`,
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer` and the hydrogen one. The same archetype config
therefore yields a different weather source across the fleet.

Either read them or refuse them.

Done when: the four agree with the rest of the fleet, and a test pins that an archetype config
naming a weather file reaches the weather component in every sizer.

title: Give air_conditioned_house one spelling of its location instead of two
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox

`air_conditioned_house` duplicates its location: a `"Seville"` string for the PV beside
`LocationEnum.SEVILLE` for the weather. One edit without the other silently desynchronizes the
two. One spelling, one place.

Related: `roadmap/p4_random_findings.md` F-7 is the same class of defect at the config level --
`PVSystemConfig.location` is a string nobody reads that can disagree with `weather_identity`.

Done when: the setup names its location once.

title: Make ModularHouseholdConfig.get_hash() round-trip stable
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, open checkbox (found 2026-09-06
while testing the reader)

`pv_azimuth: float = 180` and `pv_tilt: float = 30` hold ints in memory and come back as floats
from any JSON round trip, so a config built from defaults and the same config read from its own
file hash differently -- and the building sizer hashes configs.

Normalise in `get_hash()` (or make the defaults floats) and pin the round trip with a test.

title: Delete the json_v2 spike branch, locally and on origin
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_cleanup_todos.md, "Operational, after the stack merges"

Delete the `json_v2` spike branch, local and origin -- the parity and templating halves are
ported. (#598 itself was closed 2026-09-07.)

title: Group automatic_default_connections and air_conditioned_house once their couplings are pinned
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md, item 5 ("Still open, and
untouched by the 2026-09-07 pass")

`automatic_default_connections` and `air_conditioned_house` are small, but each carries one
environment coupling to pin first: the hplib database for the former, the reference-temperature
CSV plus the duplicated location for the latter. Neither reads a module configuration, so neither
has an axis a probe list could stand on until the coupling above it is pinned.

The worklist also names one axis shared by all twenty-two setups and belonging to no single one:
every `setup_function` invents its own parameters when `my_simulation_parameters is None`, so the
no-parameters-file path is a configuration of its own. The recorded twins all pin an explicit
parameters file, which is the right answer; the axis is named so nobody mistakes the twins for
covering it.

Depends on the air_conditioned_house location fix.

Done when: the couplings are pinned and both setups either carry a probe list and a grouped file
or are documented as deliberately flat.

title: P5: RenoVisor, building sizer and HPC harness all run from energy-system files
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, section P5 ("Consumer integration (outline;
document later)"), three unchecked items; epic.md EAC5

* RenoVisor: base file per heating system; `mapping.py` -> overrides + group flags;
  post-processing selection moves to the simulation-parameters file. (Largely delivered by the v2
  translator, which selects the recorded grouped twins through `translate.BaseFiles` -- confirm
  and tick.)
* Building sizer: same path; `ModularHouseholdConfig`, `EnergySystemConfig` and `ArcheTypeConfig`
  are deleted.
* HPC harness: payload = energy-system string + simulation parameters; the worker loads from the
  string.

EAC5 is the acceptance criterion: all three run from energy-system files and
`ModularHouseholdConfig` is deleted.

P5 also closes EQ1 (the name freeze): preset, field and fact names may change freely until P5 is
accepted; from then on a rename is a breaking change with a `schema_version` bump and a migration
note, no alias table, and a wire-format test pins every released name (EAC6).

A P5 requirements document is to be written; the list above is the outline.

title: P6: retire the parity rig and promote the setups its evidence earned into the gate
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, section P6, five unchecked items;
p3_recording_requirements.md R11.8/R11.9 (amended 2026-08-31) and AC-P3.20

Entry condition: P1, P2, P2.1, P3, P4 and P5 are all merged. Until then the rig is dispatched by
every batch that re-records, and its renaming tables are kept current.

* Confirm the whole stack is green with the rig still in place, over every runnable window (July
  is fenced pending `roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md`; R11.5 as amended 2026-09-06).
* Decide which setups earned a place in the permanent gate, on the rig's accumulated evidence --
  the six the 2026-08-28 scan cleared are the candidates, not the answer.
* Add those to `scripts/golden_config.json` and bless their references.
* Delete `.github/workflows/p3-parity.yml`, `scripts/p3_parity_*.py` and the renaming tables.
* Confirm the repository contains no reference to any of it (AC-P3.20).

Accumulated evidence so far: fleet-wide dispatches on 2026-09-18 (8f619e4a) and 2026-09-19
(dd6cb78b) were both green -- twenty-two triples each, January window, `rel_tol` and `abs_tol`
both zero, so every recorded setup reproduced its Python original at exact equality. The
candidates for the permanent gate are now every setup, which makes the question one of cost
rather than of trust.

`roadmap/p3_cleanup_todos.md`'s expectation of "seven KPI-broken setups" no longer holds: there
are none, and the baseline the rig leaves behind is full parity rather than a list of exceptions.

title: Implement the Many aggregator so a law can read several providers
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, parking lot row "Many-cardinality laws (epic
E3, P1 leaves the hook)"; epic.md EQ2 (open); p1_implementation_spec.md (E-07);
p4_component_sweep_requirements.md R2.2 under D-15 (b); p4_class_survey.md item 5

`Many(Size.PV_PEAK_POWER_IN_WATT)` is a `_ManyTerm` whose `facts_read()` returns
`(fact, Cardinality.MANY)` and whose `evaluate` raises E-07
`NotImplementedError("many-cardinality is declared but not implemented; see plan parking lot")`
(`hisim/config/laws.py:225-228`). `SizingContext` stays a frozen dataclass of typed scalars; the
tuple side-table was not added.

The named trigger: the first real consumer -- a buffer storage over a hybrid generator pair, or a
battery / price signal over several PVs. D-15 (b) names a second: the meter half of batch B2
wants `gas_loadtype` copied from the connected generator's energy carrier, which is
many-cardinality with a consistency aggregator, so the meters keep a plain field selected by the
preset instead.

EQ2 is the undecided question above it: is deferring until the first real consumer acceptable, or
must P1 ship it? The recommendation is (a) defer -- the inventory found zero readers that consume
several providers today, the file syntax (a list under `sizing_sources`) is fixed by E3
regardless, and implementing it means a `many` term, a tuple side-table, `sum`/`max`/`count`
aggregates, about 100 lines plus tests, validated on a fabricated use case. No `[decided]` marker
has been recorded, and the plan's parking lot already behaves as if (a) were taken.

Done when: the decision is recorded and, if (a) stands, this issue waits on its trigger.

title: Give Sizable enum fields a name-based decoder so a wire value becomes the enum member
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] `Sizable[SomeEnum]`
fields bypass dataclasses_json's enum handling"; p4_component_sweep_requirements.md R2.2 under
D-15 (b)

The field-level decoder that `sized_field` injects replaces the library's default decoding, so a
JSON `"FLOORHEATING"` stays a string instead of becoming the enum member. It works today only
because config enums are `(str, Enum)` with value == member name, so equality comparisons still
hold -- but `is` comparisons would silently fail. `HeatDistributionConfig.heating_system` is the
live instance.

R2.2 names the same thing from the other direction and adds the concrete mismatch: `_sizable_decoder`
coerces by value, and `LoadTypes.GAS` is `"Gas"` while the twins write `GAS`. So the meter half of
batch B2 under D-15 (b) needs a name-based decoder before an enum-typed sizable field can carry a
carrier.

Done when: `sized_field` captures the field's concrete type (or the scenario codec handles
`Sizable` unions) so an enum-typed sizable field decodes to the member, and a test pins an `is`
comparison.

several small SizingContexts instead of one"

(`SizingContext.for_building(...)` plus `.with_facts(...)` enrichment) and thread it -- that is

title: Correct the four config_defaults_spec statements the spike disproved
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, the four `[spec]` entries;
target document `system_docs/config_defaults_spec.md` section 4.1 and the design-B weakness note

1. One lazy import is unavoidable in the sizing module layout. Section 4.1 says `hisim/sizing.py`
   imports `building_config.py` directly, "no lazy imports needed" -- but `component.py` must
   import the sizing machinery and `building_config.py` imports `component.py`, so a module-level
   `sizing -> building_config` would close the cycle. The implemented resolution:
   `SizingContext.for_building` imports the building package locally.
2. Per-preset law variation exists in production after all. The weakness note claims "no such
   variation exists today", but `GenericBoilerConfig`'s scaled factories disagree on the minimal
   power law per fuel: gas/oil/hydrogen use a constant 0, pellet and wood chip use one twelfth of
   the sized maximal power. The escape hatch the spec sketched -- a preset assigning a
   `SizingLaw` as a field value -- is implemented, not hypothetical.
3. `sizing.concrete(value)`, the typed pass-through with a runtime assertion used at the pilot
   read sites, belongs in section 4.1; so does `Sizable` being widened to include `SizingLaw`,
   since the per-preset escape hatch makes law values legal field content pre-resolution.
4. The dataclass field-ordering constraint fires on every converted class (trailing capex fields
   need `None` defaults once sized fields above them are defaulted) -- worth stating so the sweep
   expects it.

Done when: section 4.1 and the weakness note say what the code does.

title: Decide whether contributed facts need a CONNECTED scope for multi-loop systems
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[spec] The HDS controller's
sizing facts are scope-GLOBAL, unlike the boiler's CONNECTED power band"

Surfaced by auditing a `ResolutionReport` of the heat-pump building-sizer chain:
`HeatDistributionControllerConfig.SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` declares `water_mass_flow_rate...` and
`heat_distribution_system_type` without a scope, i.e. GLOBAL -- two heat-distribution loops in
one scenario would hard-error on the double contribution rather than resolve per loop.
Defensible today (one HDS per building) and loud rather than wrong, but it is a modelling
decision the CONNECTED alternative would make differently.

The epic's decision register records that B11 ("Scope rule GLOBAL vs CONNECTED for contributed
facts") was superseded on 2026-08-25: no scopes exist any more; every fact is `<name>.<fact>` and
ambiguity is per consumer.

Worth an explicit look when multi-loop or multi-building scenarios reach the engine -- which is
the named trigger, the same one as the multi-zone `Building` row of the plan's parking lot.

A concrete near-miss is recorded as `roadmap/p4_random_findings.md` F-23: two sibling generator
controllers read the emitter circuit's contributed heating threshold while
`ElectricHeatingControllerConfig` re-derives it, because direct electric heating has no water
circuit and no provider exists -- so a system with both an emitter controller and an electric
heater would diverge the moment an author pins the emitter threshold by hand.

description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/plan.md, parking lot rows "Multi-zone `Building`,

The template / repeat layer (a preprocessor to a flat file) is the second parking-lot row with

The two process-wide strings left too: `RESULT_SCENARIO_NAME` and `DESCRIPTION` became

title: Make @constructor stamp provenance with the arguments it was called with
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-3 ("`@constructor` never stamps provenance", reported,
Open)

Only `@preset` writes the provenance attribute (`hisim/config/presets.py:_declare`), and the
stamp carries a builder name with no arguments. A recorder can therefore never emit a
`constructor:` entry, and P3's R2.2 and spec section 3.4 are preset-only in practice. Recording a
constructor entry needs the stamp to carry the arguments it was called with.

The finding places the work in P1's kernel, not in P3.

The constructors this blocks are the identifier-lookup ones of Q-P2.6: weather `for_location`,
occupancy `for_household`, building `for_tabula_code`.

Done when: a config built through a declared constructor records as `constructor: <name>` with
its arguments, and a twin using one re-records to itself.

title: Give golden_validate.py --scan-all a deterministic verdict or retire the flag
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-16 (reported, Open)

In a full 21-setup scan, `automatic_default_connections` and
`household_district_heating_building_sizer` were reported non-deterministic (12 and 16 differing
KPIs), yet both PASS when re-run in isolation with `--setup`. This is cross-run LPG/cache
interference inside one long scan session, not a property of the setups.

Consequence: `--scan-all` is unusable as a gate, and the eligibility table in
`roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/p3_setup_inventory.md` section 4f -- which came from one such
scan -- should be read as indicative, not authoritative. Per-setup runs are the reliable form.

Read together with F-21, the pattern is the same: this fleet's tooling is reliable per-setup and
flaky in bulk.

Done when: either each setup in a scan gets its own isolated cache so a scan equals the sum of
its per-setup runs, or `--scan-all` is removed and the inventory table is re-derived per setup.

title: Give the golden gate an absolute tolerance floor so a physically zero KPI is comparable
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-21 (verified, Open) and F-31; `golden_ref_spec.md`
section 7

A full-fleet `golden_check.py` run fails one pair of sixteen:
`household_electric_heating_building_sizer / one_week_60s`, on the KPI "Temperature deviation ...
below set temperature 20.0 Celsius" -- `ref = 1.216772342142273e-09`,
`got = 1.2167721052946946e-09`. The absolute difference is 2.4e-16, the relative difference is
1.95e-7, which exceeds `rel_tol = 1e-9` by a factor of about 195. The gate's report prints
"rel diff=0.000%", which rounds the number that decides the verdict out of view.

The cause is the tolerance regime, not the code: `golden_ref_spec.md` section 7 fixes
`rel_tol = 1e-9, abs_tol = 0` on the reasoning that it "absorbs sub-ULP platform noise". That
holds for KPIs of ordinary magnitude and fails exactly for KPIs that are physically zero -- here
a temperature deviation of 1.2e-9 degC.h -- where a relative comparison has nothing to be
relative to and one last-bit difference is an infinite relative error.

F-31 proved it is one ULP against `abs_tol = 0` and that which way it falls depends on cache
state, not on code: the pair passes in isolation on the documents branch and fails in isolation
on the implementation branch, bit-identically, and reverting the only two golden-path files
leaves the failure unchanged. Nothing was re-blessed.

Done when: an `abs_tol` floor (even 1e-12) makes near-zero KPIs comparable, the spec's section 7
states it, and the report prints the number that decides the verdict.

title: Make the EMS refuse its two duplicate weight-2 electricity target outputs
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-25 ("a latent twin of F-24, deliberately left alone",
Open)

`L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem.__init__` creates two `HEAT_PUMP_BUILDING` +
`ELECTRICITY_TARGET` weight-2 outputs, one for `HeatPumpHplib` and one for
`MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib`. It is harmless today only because pruning removes whichever class is
absent. A symmetric guard on the imperative path would fail every EMS setup at construction, so
it was left visible rather than hidden.

F-24 is the fixed sibling: two outputs answering one `(tags, weight)` search made the dispatch
list one entry too long and paired the battery's input with the heat-pump-DHW output, measured as
battery charging 32.09 -> 0.0 kWh and 62 of 108 KPIs moved. Guard `EF-2B` (ambiguous dispatch
signal) now refuses that shape on the declarative path.

Note that P4 F-1 (fixed 2026-09-12) removed the constructor's phantom target outputs entirely and
moved target creation into `connect_with_dynamic_connections_list`, so check whether this
duplicate still exists before doing the work.

Done when: the EMS declares one target per participant kind, and the imperative path refuses two
ports answering one signal as `EF-2B` does.

title: Enforce carrier and unit at imperative wiring time, as the declarative path already does
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-36 (reported, "To be fixed later, as its own change")

The two build paths share one participant vocabulary -- every aggregator's `CHANNELS` declaration
-- but only the declarative path enforces the whole declaration. A feed resolved from an
energy-system file passes `ChannelMatcher.match_and_validate`, which checks tags, carrier and
unit: a power output feeding an energy channel is refused with `EF-30`
(`tests/test_meter_channels.py::test_the_matcher_refuses_a_feed_in_the_wrong_unit` pins exactly
that -- a WATT feed into `FuelMeter`'s WATT_HOUR consumption channel). The imperative path checks
none of it: `add_component_input_and_connect` records tags and unit on the created port, and
`get_channel_inputs` selects participants by tag subset alone, so the byte-identical wiring the
declarative path refuses is silently accepted when a setup writes it by hand.

Concretely, using the repository's own pinned example: wire a heat source whose output is
HEAT_CONSUMPTION-tagged but denominated in WATT into the fuel meter imperatively, and
`i_simulate` sums watts as watt-hours -- at 60-second resolution the priced fuel energy is
overstated sixtyfold, a plausible-looking number that means nothing.

The finding names the seam: unit/carrier validation at imperative wiring time, where the matched
channel is known, not inside `get_channel_inputs` -- a lookup that silently drops mismatched
inputs would trade a wrong sum for a silently smaller one. The blast radius over existing setups
is unknown until tried, which is why it is a finding and not a patch.

title: Stop a failed recording leaving an uncommittable file in energy_systems/
description:
Source: roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-34 (verified, Open)

`scripts/record_all_setups.py` writes the file and then verifies it builds, and on failure leaves
it "in place for inspection" -- so after a failed run an untracked
`energy_systems/<stem>.energy_system.yaml` sits there that must never be committed. Sensible for
debugging, hazardous next to `git add -A`.

Done when: a failed recording writes to a scratch path, or the file is named so `.gitignore`
catches it.

title: Decide how *.simulation.json should carry EconomicParameters
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 5; cost_spec.md section 11 Q3 (Phase 1)

`SimulationParameters` has a custom `__init__` and its JSONWizard field list does not include
e.g. `country`. To stay strictly additive (identical `*.simulation.json` round-trips),
`economic_parameters` is a plain attribute (default None) set via keyword argument or
`set_economic_parameters()`, not a dataclass field.

A follow-up decision is needed on how `*.simulation.json` should carry it. Spec Q3 proposes
serializing it there, for reproducibility -- which changes the JSON schema of simulation files.

Note: the declarative path has `*.simulation.yaml` files now, so the question is really about
both parameter formats.

Done when: the decision is taken and, if serialization wins, the two parameter formats carry the
block and round-trip.

title: Merge the namespaced lifecycle KPIs into all_kpis.json at cutover
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 6 and 7

Item 6: the new namespaced lifecycle KPIs are written to `lifecycle_kpis.json`, not merged into
`all_kpis.json`, so the legacy KPI JSON stays byte-identical during the parallel phase. The spec
(section 7.3) is ambiguous on whether new names should already appear in the existing KPI
collection; merging them in is a one-line change at cutover.

Item 7, the half that lands with it: `KpiEntry` gained optional `value_min`/`value_max` fields
(spec section 7.3), and dataclass-wizard emits `null` for unset optional fields, so
`all_kpis.json` gains two null keys per entry. This is the one visible (backward-compatible)
change to a legacy artifact; if the JSON golden parity check diffs byte-wise it must be
re-baselined once.

Done when: the cutover happens, the merge lands, and the golden re-baseline is one deliberate
commit.

title: Decide whether a capacity tariff at 3600 s timesteps should fail or be approximated
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 9

`BillingDeterminants` peaks are computed from the meter's power series in postprocessing. If
`seconds_per_timestep` does not divide the billing interval the pre-check fails per spec section
8.4. For setups with 3600 s timesteps and 15-minute intervals this means capacity tariffs simply
cannot be billed.

The source asks: acceptable? (Spec says fail; implemented as fail.)

Done when: the owner confirms the failure, or an approximation with a stated error is allowed.

title: Support simulations longer than a year in the lifecycle engine, or refuse them
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 15

Simulations shorter than a year are annualized by linear extrapolation with a warning (spec
section 3.6 rule 5). Simulations longer than a year are not supported by the lifecycle engine:
the first simulated year is used and a warning is emitted. The spec is silent on multi-year
simulations.

Done when: the spec says what a multi-year simulation means economically, and the engine either
implements it or refuses by name instead of silently using year one.

title: Give a meter a simulated_cost_in_euro hand-off so dynamic tariffs are integrated in-run
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 16 and 17, with the reporting consequence in 29

Item 16: dynamic-tariff in-simulation cost integration (spec section 8.4) is implemented in
postprocessing from the meter power series and the contract's spot series (native resolution).
The optional `simulated_cost_in_euro` hand-off from a meter that already integrated cost during
simulation is honored when present, but no meter currently computes it.

Item 17: the `TariffProvider` component publishes price signals per timestep; the price forecast
publication mirrors what `generic_price_signal.py` does today (24 h horizon). Whether MPC should
consume the new provider already in the parallel phase is a control-side decision (the spec keeps
EMS work out of scope).

Item 29 records the reporting cost: the section 8.5 dynamic-tariff decomposition
(volume/flexibility/capacity) has no report section because no shipped example runs a dynamic
contract yet. The synthetic contract exists; a meter-side cost-integration example is the missing
piece.

Done when: one meter computes `simulated_cost_in_euro` under a dynamic contract, a shipped
example runs it, and the section 8.5 report block exists.

title: Decide whether *_gross perspectives should exclude the anyway-cost credit
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 32, modelling note (b)

The anyway credit is currently booked in gross views too, while spec section 4.1 ties it to the
differential comparison. Worth a review whether `*_gross` perspectives should exclude it -- the
credit is separately reported either way.

Context from the same item: in the German worked example the year-2 "residual value" drop is
58 kEUR of ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT, because the old wall/windows/top-ceiling (1988/1993/1988) have
exactly two years of life left at the 2026 price basis, so section 4.1 books the avoided
like-for-like renovation at year 2.

Done when: the owner decides, the perspectives implement it, and the report goldens move once.

title: Decide whether a weather-year and price-basis-year mismatch gets a report header note
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 28, closing "Open question"

With the economic clock (2026-07-07), subsidy scheme validity, the CO2-price-path anchor and
existing-asset ages follow the price basis year (the economic "today") instead of the possibly
historical weather year -- a 2021 weather year with 2026 economics previously found no valid
2024+ schemes.

Open question: should `WEATHER_YEAR != PRICE_BASIS_YEAR` emit an advisory note in the report
header? It is currently only visible in the parameters line.

Done when: the owner decides and the report does or does not carry the note.

title: Wire or delete the REDUCED_VAT benefit kind, which has no consumer
description:
Source: roadmap/cost-spec-v2.md section 7, discrepancy B7 ("Still open"), and section 8 decision
D1

`REDUCED_VAT` / `PayoutKind.VAT_REDUCTION` awards have no consumer anywhere. W2.2 (commit
d0f6ffe4) typed the payload as `ReducedVatBenefit(vat_rate)` and documented it as unwired at both
ends (the dataclass at `hisim/economics/subsidies/catalog.py:377` and the award branch at
`solver.py:337`), deliberately neither wiring nor deleting it. D1 says: leave typed, unwired;
wiring is a methodology question deferred until a real scheme needs it.

Decide: wire into `_eligible_cost_basis` VAT netting, or delete the kind.

Related: the VAT reclassification of the migrated price entries (cost_spec Q5) is the methodology
this depends on.

title: Make the subsidy solver and the financing module agree on the repayment-grant basis
description:
Source: roadmap/cost-spec-v2.md section 7, discrepancy B3 ("Fix in W3.2")

The solver values a repayment grant on the gross measure cost
(`hisim/economics/subsidies/solver.py:427-429`, `value += gross * award.loan_repayment_grant_share`)
while financing applies `repayment_grant_share` to the principal
(`hisim/economics/calculators/financing_application.py`, whose own docstring at :26 says "section
7 B3 is preserved, unfixed"). The solver therefore overstates soft loans whenever
`financed_share < 1`; it is masked today because the shipped KfW rate is 0.0.

Done when: one basis is chosen, both sides use it, and a test with `financed_share < 1` pins the
agreement.

title: Settle the six remaining open questions of the cost engine implementation plan
description:
Source: roadmap/cost-spec-v2.md section 6, "Open questions for review"

Six of the eight are still open (2 is resolved behaviourally, 8 is decided and implemented):

1. Package layout depth (section 2.5): sub-packages as proposed, or a flat module with enforced
   import-lint layers only? The import audit shrinks the question -- only `bridge.py`,
   `scenarios.py`, `__main__.py` and the tests import the evaluator. Recommendation: import-lint
   contracts from day 1, physical sub-packages once seam 3 has settled the calculator boundaries.
   Question 2 adds: the physical `data/` vs `engine/` move inside `subsidies.py` is the one thing
   left of seam 2, deferred so importers churn once.
3. Long-timeline examples (section 3.2): individual row labels vs a labelled two-column table
   convention -- decide when the first 40-year example appears.
4. Tolerance policy: a default `abs_tol` per unit (0.01 EUR for money, 1e-6 for rates),
   overridable per cell, or always explicit as currently specified?
5. Which existing tests migrate into the worked-example format vs stay as plain pytest. (The
   VDI-2067 hand examples in `test_economics_engine.py` are the natural first migrations.)
6. Tariff contracts in `economic_inputs.json` (W1.4): embed full contracts vs reference-by-id
   plus an explicit catalog version stamp?
7. Fix-or-freeze decisions for section 7 -- each needs an owner and a call before worked examples
   freeze the affected path. (B3 and B7 are the two still open; see their own issues.)

description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H8; hisim/subsidy_catalog/README_IE.md;
roadmap/renovisor/implementation/step11_irish_subsidy_catalogue.md

title: Add a TIERED_PER_UNIT benefit kind so the SEAI solar PV grant is paid pro rata
description:

unit that changes by tier and is capped": `PER_UNIT` has no cap and no tiers, `LUMP_SUM` does not

schemes collapse into one that reproduces the page's own example (2.5 kWp -> 1 500 EUR).

This is a HiSim engine change, not a contract one.

`approximated` price for that emitter instead of aborting.

Needs the owner's decision. Until then the substitution stands and
`TestTheLowTemperatureRadiatorBlocker` fails the day a cost row exists.

title: Carry measures[i].cost, installation_year, applicant and scop into the request schema
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md F7 and F10 (frontend section, HiSim's half), and the
step-10 / step-12 notes under H7

HiSim reads four additive request fields that the vendored
`hisim/renovisor/contract/calculation-request.schema.json` still rejects, so they are implemented
and unreachable:

* `measures[i].cost {min_in_euro_per_m2, max_in_euro_per_m2, source}` -- without it every
  envelope subject of every real request is `unpriced: true` and
  `result.json.costs.investment_breakdown.envelope_material` is absent with the reason "the
  request carries no material price". The frontend copies `materials.yaml` `measure_costs` into
  it. HiSim already refuses a band with `min > max`, a negative price or a non-finite one as
  `measure.cost.band_invalid`, a code minted HiSim-side because section 7 of the contract does
  not carry the block yet.
* `house.<block>.installation_year` -- without it every existing asset is dated to
  `construction_year` and reported `defaulted`.
* an `applicant` block -- read when present; it carries `receives_means_tested_benefit`,
  `first_time_buyer` and `managed_full_retrofit`, without which every welfare, first-time-buyer,
  One-Stop-Shop-only and loan row of the Irish catalogue comes out `undetermined`.
* `house.heating.scop` -- the engine's subsidy conditions read a heat pump's seasonal performance
  factor as a technical attribute and neither the schema nor the recorded twins state one, so any
  scheme keyed on SCOP stays undetermined for every RenoVisor calculation. Alternative: a
  decision that no Irish scheme uses it.

Done when: the shared `calculation-request.schema.json` carries the four, HiSim re-vendors it,
and the end-to-end test shows a priced envelope subject and a dated existing asset.
close_reason: Done: the shared calculation-request.schema.json carries measures[i].cost, the ten installation_year leaves, living_area_in_m2 and applicant (renovisorissues !8), HiSim re-vendors it (specs at 93b7d70) and #789's readers are carried onto it; the end-to-end staged run prices the facade subject and dates the boiler. house.heating.scop left out: the SCOP is the W35/W55 pair of hisim-epc.27.
