Specification (2026-09-20) of the schema additions, to be written into /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/calculation-request.schema.json and calculation-request.md section 3 together with the frontend agent (F7/F10); HiSim's readers already exist. All optional, additive:
- measures[i].cost: {min_in_euro_per_m2: number >= 0, max_in_euro_per_m2: number >= min, source: string}; the frontend copies materials.yaml measure_costs; HiSim refuses min > max or negatives (measure.cost.band_invalid, exit 2).
- house.heating.installation_year, house.pv_system.installation_year, house.battery.installation_year, house.solar_thermal_system.installation_year, house.building.<facade|roof|floor|window|door>.installation_year: integer 1900..2100; default construction_year, reported defaulted.
- house.building.living_area_in_m2: number > 0; default the conditioned floor area.
- applicant: {role: owner_occupier|landlord|tenant|condominium_association, receives_means_tested_benefit: boolean, first_time_buyer: boolean, managed_full_retrofit: boolean, taxable_household_income_in_euro: number, household_size: integer, main_residence: boolean}, every key optional; absent = undetermined for the subsidy conditions that read it.

HiSim work once the schema carries them: refresh the vendored schema, mapping-report used/defaulted lines for each, capability document field probes for each new leaf, tests in test_request/test_economics_context through a real request (the readers are tested directly today), whitelist untouched. title: Accept a list of cache directories on SimulationParameters for the container
description:
Source: roadmap/renovisor/implementation/step5_parametriser_and_calculate.md ("a list of cache
directories on `SimulationParameters` -- step 7b (Q25 follow-up)"); challenges.md Q25 and C26

Q25 decided: a cache directory is mapped into the container, and HiSim's simulation parameters
accept a list of cache directories; the cache is exempt from the output-location cleanliness rule
(R13.4). C26 records why the location must be explicit: `ResultPathProviderSingleton` and the
input cache both default into the repository (`hisim/inputs/cache/Building_<hash>.cache` is on
disk on main right now), and the cache is content-keyed and deterministic, so keeping it across
calculations is wanted -- but its location must be a declared directory, not the working tree.

any of them, writes go to the first writable one, and a test proves a read-only seed directory
plus a writable one behaves as described.

RenoVisor run fills the list from HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES (os.pathsep, absolute-only) and calculation.json states the directories used; the realized parameter record deliberately stays machine-free (its own header). comments.author: noah
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-09-20: MVP. Specification:
1. SimulationParameters gains cache_directories: List[str] (default: the package's current cache location, so nothing changes for existing callers). A CacheLocations helper (class-scope constants, in the module that owns the cache path today) answers read(path_relative) = first directory holding the file, in order, and write_directory() = the first entry; every caching component goes through it — survey the six caching components hisim-hi1.2 names (building/TABULA, weather, PV, solar thermal, car, LPG/UTSP) and any other hisim/inputs/cache writer.
2. The RenoVisor run (hisim/renovisor/simulation.py) fills it from the environment variable HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES (os.pathsep-separated, absolute paths) when set; the realized simulation record and calculation.json state the directories used. Cache directories are exempt from the output-location cleanliness rule (R13.4) and from the 'no artefacts outside results/' test rule — document that in AGENTS.md.
3. Tests (base): two directories, a file present only in the second is read, a new file is written to the first; unset variable = today's behaviour. End-to-end (system_setups): the mockup baseline run twice with a temporary cache directory, the second run finds the cache (assert by file mtime or a log line), results identical.
4. Backend side (file as a B item in specs/todos.md): mount a persistent volume and pass HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES; hisim-hi1.8 (move the generated cache out of hisim/inputs) becomes the natural default location and depends on this.

title: Confirm translator.commit is filled once the backend writes hisim/COMMIT into the image
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H6, H13 and H17 (one thing under three ids)

Observed: `mapping_report.json` carries `{"version": "2.0.0", "commit": null,
"hisim_commit": null}`, and `capabilities.py` validates the capability document against a schema
requiring `translator.commit` to be a string, so a null was fatal: the probe exited 1 and the
backend registered the version `broken`. The cause was `HiSimCommit.of()` shelling out to
`git -C /app rev-parse --short HEAD` in an image whose Containerfile fetches shallow and deletes
`.git`, which forced the backend to ship the `git` binary (~100 MB) plus an 8 KB fabricated
`.git` holding only HEAD -- 1.65 GB instead of 1.55 GB purely for provenance.

HiSim's half is done. `HiSimCommit.of()` in `hisim/renovisor/report.py` now reads the file
`hisim/COMMIT` next to the package, then the `HISIM_COMMIT` environment variable, then git as the
last fallback, and it feeds the mapping report, the capability document and
`economics_result.json` alike; the repository's `Dockerfile` writes that file from a
`HISIM_COMMIT` build argument; and the capability document now emits `"unknown"` instead of
`null`, because the vendored contract schema types both commit fields as strings.

What is left is not HiSim's code. The backend does not build with HiSim's Dockerfile (it
generates its own Containerfile), so the `ARG HISIM_COMMIT` there is irrelevant to the released
images; the backend agent writes `hisim/COMMIT` in its build stage from the SHA it already
resolves. Once it does, the `.git` stub and the runtime git binary can go.

Done when: a released image's `mapping_report.json` and capability document both carry a real
commit, verified on a run, and the three shared-todo boxes are ticked.
close_reason: Backend confirmed on image v20260923-1 (HiSim 75877861): capability document, mapping_report.json and economics_result.json all carry commit 7587786 without git in the image (renovisorissues #10).

title: Carry heat pump SCOP and its W35/W55 application in the house inventory spec
description:
Source: owner conversation 2026-09-21 on heat pump efficiency; the maintainer of the RenoVisor house
inventory spec (calculation-request.schema.json and calculation-request.md in
/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/) will carry the fields, HiSim does not write that spec.

Today the request has `house.heating.seasonal_efficiency_in_percent` (1..400) and HiSim applies it to
boilers only. For a heat pump the translator lists it as not implemented and the twin's hplib
defaults stand. The field also does not say which number a heat pump user would enter: SCOP x 100
(about 300..500) or the ErP label's eta_s (about 120..200), which differ by a factor of about 2.5.

What HiSim needs the spec to carry for a heat pump (existing one in `house.heating`, and the same
shape on the `heating_system` measure options for a new one):
- `scop`: number > 1, the manufacturer's standardized seasonal COP per EN 14825, average climate.
- `scop_application`: enum `w35` | `w55`, the sink temperature the label refers to (low-temperature
  or medium-temperature application). Without it the number cannot be placed on the curve.
- Ground source: same two fields; the standard's brine bins apply. Nothing extra.
- The boiler keeps `seasonal_efficiency_in_percent`; the spec should say the percent field is not
  meant for heat pumps.

This also settles the `house.heating.scop` item in hisim-epc.14 (subsidy conditions read the SCOP as
a technical attribute): one field serves both the physics and the economics.

Done when: the shared schema and the request document carry the two fields with the meaning above,
and HiSim has re-vendored the schema (hisim-epc.14 covers the re-vendoring routine).
close_reason: Done: the request carries house.heating.heatpump_scop_en14825_w35/_w55 (renovisorissues !9, re-vendored at 93b7d70); HiSim refuses them on a heating that is not a heat pump (heating.scop.not_a_heat_pump) and a W55 above W35 (heating.scop.w55_above_w35), lists both as not_implemented_yet (tracked hisim-4g9.15) and probes them on a heat pump. Physics only (decision 2026-09-23): nothing is published for subsidies, since no grant is ever decided for the pump already in the house.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Contract PR #10 (ffe1304, 2026-09-22) added the SCOP, in a different shape from this bead's: homeinventory.yaml energy_system_config.heating_system carries heatpump_scop_en14825_w35 and heatpump_scop_en14825_w55 (both nullable numbers, EN 14825 average climate, SCOP not eta_s or JAZ; give both where the fiche has both, W35 alone for a low-temperature unit) beside heatpump_flow_temperature_in_celsius. title: Caching correctness and the cache service
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md, roadmap/cache_service_spec.md, roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-8

Everything about how HiSim caches computed inputs: the six components that use
`hisim.utils.get_cache_file`, the producer-keyed cache service (phase 1 landed for weather, PV
series and building solar gains), the legacy caches that still key on configuration alone, the
non-bit-exact PV CSV round trip, the pylpg serialisation workaround, and the cache service's own
open questions.

title: Read the building-sizer cache directories from the environment instead of cluster paths
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 4

All `system_setups/household_*_building_sizer.py` hard-code FZJ cluster paths, still on main
(checked 2026-09-20):
`cache_dir_path_simuparams = "/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/hisim_inputs_cache/"` and
`cache_dir_path_utsp: Optional[str] = "/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/lpg-utsp-cache"`.

On any machine that is not the cluster these paths silently do not exist and caching is disabled
-- every run recomputes LPG profiles and weather inputs, which dominates runtime for short
simulations. The RenoVisor use case runs one simulation per request, so cold caches hurt every
single request.

Suggested fix: read the cache directories from environment variables (e.g.
`HISIM_UTSP_CACHE_DIR`, `HISIM_INPUTS_CACHE_DIR`) or from `SimulationParameters`, with the
cluster paths as documented defaults. One shared helper instead of a copy in each of the eleven
setups.

Related: `roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md` names the two
`/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/` existence probes as environment couplings a recording has to pin;
and the RenoVisor container needs a declared cache-directory list anyway.

Testing: a setup-level test that sets the env var to a temp dir and asserts the occupancy config
picks it up; run one of the fast marker tests twice and assert the second run hits the cache.

title: Run the cold-versus-cached protocol over all six caching components
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 13 ("Every component that caches, not just this one")
and section 10 ("How to verify a fix")

The worst fault of the pylpg investigation (Fault D, section 6) is a caching pattern: a key taken
from what the caller asked for, contents produced by what the code actually did. Nothing about it
is specific to load profiles, so the verification protocol belongs to every cached component, and
each needs its own answer to one question -- can this cache ever be filled with something other
than what its key describes?

Six components use the shared helper `hisim.utils.get_cache_file`:
`loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py` (occupancy profiles; Faults A-D, the only one that
rewrites its own configuration), `generic_pv_system.py` (a year of AC power ratios; second
confirmed defect, see the CSV round-trip issue), `weather.py` (weather series; feeds nearly every
setup), `building/building.py` (building physics), `solar_thermal_system.py` (collector output)
and `generic_car.py` (car profiles; its data originates from the occupancy, so Fault D can reach
it second-hand).

What the sweep should produce, for each of the six in that order: run the protocol, and record
whether run 1 and run 2 agree bit for bit. Where they differ, establish which of the two is right
-- the cached or the computed value -- because that decides whether the fix is in the writer or
the reader. Then answer, per component, whether every input that changes the result is part of
the key. A cache whose key omits a relevant input is Fault D wearing a different hat.

PV is expected to fail today, which makes it the first thing to measure rather than a surprise to
discover.

title: Stop the PV cache round-tripping float64 through CSV text
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 13, "The PV cache does not round-trip exactly"; with
the consequence recorded as roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-32

`hisim/components/generic_pv_system/pv_system.py` writes its cache with `database.to_csv(...)`
(:514) and reads it back with `pd.read_csv(...)` (:485) -- a text round trip of float64 data. So
a cached PV run and an uncached one are not the same run.

P3's parity work already ran into it: giving both sides of a comparison one cache directory let
the second run read the first run's PV output back out of the CSV, which both masked a real
configuration difference and invented a false one. That was worked around there by giving each
side its own empty cache; it is not fixed. F-32 generalises it: any A/B comparison of two HiSim
runs on one machine has this hazard.

Done when: the PV cache round-trips bit-exactly (parquet, npy, or a full-precision text format),
and the cold-versus-cached protocol passes for PV.

title: Key the solar thermal and car caches on their producer code, not configuration alone
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-8 (fixed for three producers), closing paragraph;
roadmap/cache_service_spec.md section 12 (the survey)

Phase 1 of the cache service landed three producers that key on their own code:
`hisim/components/weather/calculation.py` (`weather_series`),
`hisim/components/generic_pv_system/calculation.py` (`pv_series`) and
`hisim/components/building/solar_gains.py` (`building_solar_gains`). Each key is a fingerprint of
the producer module's source and of every `hisim` module in its transitive import closure, plus
the third-party versions in it and the calculation's DTO.

Two legacy caches still key on configuration and simulation parameters alone:
`solar_thermal_system.py` (pvlib solar positions, so a pvlib upgrade is what would be invisible)
and `generic_car.py` (an LPG export resampled by our own `resample_meters_driven`). Both are
future producers; the survey in section 12 of the cache spec lists them.

Why it matters, from F-8: before the producers, a physics change (the zenith clamp of #628, which
moves 33 KPIs on a cold cache) was invisible to the golden gate, because CI restores
`hisim/inputs/cache` from the previous run and the restore key hashes only the files that decide
where an entry is filed, not the ones that decide what is in it.

Done when: both caches are producer-keyed and an edit to either producer misses the cache.

title: Delete the whole-calculation pylpg lock once the cache service removes the need for it
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 9, F13 ("shipped in #611, and meant to be deleted")

Since F12 did not end the sqlite contention and the remaining shared route was never found, the
lock F10 introduced is held for the length of a calculation, so local LPG runs serialise. Of the
twenty-two system setups four run local profiles, so eighteen keep their parallelism and four
take turns -- and those four were contending with each other in any case.

The document is explicit: this is a workaround for a defect in a third-party binary, and it
should be deleted rather than maintained. The cache service (PR #584) removes the need to
generate the same profile repeatedly at all, which is the real answer; when it lands, the
serialisation goes with the need for it. The lock's docstring says so too, so whoever finds it
does not mistake it for design.

Done when: the cache service makes repeated generation unnecessary and the whole-calculation lock
is removed, keeping F10's install lock.

title: Find the shared path by which two pylpg calculations still reach one sqlite database
description:

With F12 in place each calculation runs its own executable beside its own `profilegenerator.db3`,
and one still died with `database is locked`. Some path -- an absolute location compiled in, a
temp directory, a user-profile location -- is shared and was not found. F13 serialises around it.

The document records it as "recorded rather than pursued": the question only matters if the
serialisation ever has to be lifted before the cache service makes it moot.

needs-triage: this is an investigation with no owner and a named reason not to do it. Close it
with the F13 lock removal if the cache service lands first.

title: Answer the four open questions of the cache service spec
description:
Source: roadmap/cache_service_spec.md section 13, "Open questions"

1. Blob size cap and total quota -- needs measured sizes of the largest current `.cache` files
   (UTSP full-year minutely results are the likely maximum).
2. Does the internal endpoint require read auth? Recommendation: no -- friction for zero gain
   inside the institute network.
3. Which weather subset stays bundled in the repository for offline-after-install use?
4. Should the RenoVisor container prewarm at build time (bigger image, instant start) or at first
   start (small image, slow first request)? Recommendation: build time for weather datasets,
   first-start for opportunistic entries.

Related: the deferred cache writes of section 12 (PV non-predictive, building and solar thermal
fill their cache late) go with the producer migration.

title: Move the generated cache out of hisim/inputs so it stops masquerading as input data
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3, "Separate tracked
reference data from generated cache"; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C26

working tree.

title: Close the fourteen PRICED component classes that no cost facts source can price
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 34 (2026-09-08, stack part 8/8 review)

Fourteen component classes declare `cost_relevance = CostRelevance.PRICED` while nothing can
produce `ComponentCostFacts` for them -- no `get_cost_facts()` of their own and no entry in
`adapter.FactsExtractors.BY_CLASS_NAME`. Each fails `Simulator.check_cost_declarations` before
the first timestep of any run that asks for lifecycle costs, and would fail the postprocessing D7
check if it got that far. Closing one means two things: a `devices_<COUNTRY>.json` row with real
sources in `sources.json` for the device type it is priced against, and an adapter entry (or a
hook) mapping its config to that asset class and a size.

Grouped by the device type the cost database lacks:

* CHP -- `advanced_fuel_cell.CHP`, `generic_chp.SimpleCHP`. No CHP device type exists at all.
  This is why `system_setups/dynamic_components.py` fails fast under all options: it wires two
  CHPs and the run is refused before the first timestep.
* Fuel cell -- `generic_fuel_cell.FuelCell` (the reversible cell moved to `obsolete/components/`
  under D-25 on 2026-09-11).
* Electrolyzers other than the migrated one -- `generic_electrolyzer.GenericElectrolyzer`,
  `generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.AdvancedElectrolyzer`. The `ELECTROLYZER` device type now
  exists, so these two need an adapter entry each -- but only after someone checks that their
  configs state a rating in kW and that an industrial PEM price is the right one.
* Hydrogen storage -- `generic_hydrogen_storage.GenericHydrogenStorage`,
  `generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.HydrogenStorage`. No hydrogen-storage device type.
* Mobility -- `generic_car.Car`, `advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery`. No car or car-battery
  device type; the stationary `BATTERY` entry is not a vehicle pack.
* Wind -- `generic_windturbine.Windturbine`. No wind device type.
* Air conditioning -- `air_conditioner.AirConditioner`, `simple_air_conditioner.SimpleAirConditioner`.
  No air-conditioner device type.

title: Reclassify every migrated price as net and set its true VAT handling
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md "Spec open questions (section 11)" Q5 and "New issues" 4;
cost_spec.md section 11 Q5 (Phase 3)

Device entries migrated from `configuration.py` carry `vat_rate: 0.19` (DE) / `0.20` (AT) and are

with an EXPERT_ESTIMATE source, so macroeconomic results for migrated data are approximate.

gross up, macroeconomic uses net directly, VAT-reduction subsidies override the rate. Requires
touching every price entry once during data migration.

title: Fix the pellet and wood-chip emission factors quoted per kWh against per-ton prices

the factors recorded in the entry notes -- so the emission factors are the half left behind.

title: Make self.config precisely typed per component so mypy sees the 300 masked findings
description:
Source: roadmap/json_development/json_cleanup.md section 6, "Mypy visibility for config classes
(follow-up to sweep 1)"

Removing the dataclass-wizard's `Any` base revealed about 300 latent typing findings that sweep 1
deliberately re-masked to stay reviewable: LSP-violating `get_cost_capex(config: SpecificConfig)`
overrides (about 75), subclass-field reads and writes on `ConfigBase`-typed slots (about 280),
and a handful of genuine type lies (`my_module_config` holding a dict, the `List[int]` annotation
on `post_processing_options` that actually holds enum members).

The real fix is a generic `Component[TConfig]` so `self.config` is precisely typed per component,
then: delete the checking-only escape hatches on `ConfigBase` (the `__getattr__`/`__setattr__`
and serialization-API stubs), re-enable the `override` error code, and drop
`follow_imports = skip` for `dataclasses_json` -- which restores the injected-API stubs problem,
to be solved via a small typing shim or upstream stubs.

Related, and unblocked by the same change: the config-presets findings note that
`Catalog` attribute access is inherently `Any` because a `ClassVar` may not contain a type
variable, so `Catalog` cannot be generic over the config class it serves; a
`__class_getitem__`-based `Catalog[SomeConfig]` declared as a plain class attribute might work
once the `Component[TConfig]` generics sweep lands.

Also named there: `my_sim.my_module_config` holding a dict is one of the type lies -- see the
issue that settles what that attribute may hold.

title: Purge or repair the fourteen components that cannot be built from their own defaults

Source: roadmap/json_development/json_cleanup.md section 2, "Purge or repair the unbuildable

title: Re-enable pylint's cyclic-import check by moving for_building into the building package
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] pylint's
`cyclic-import` cannot see the difference between a lazy import and a real one"

`SizingContext.for_building` imports the building package inside the method body, which is
invisible to Python's import system but fully visible to pylint's import graph, so prospector
reports the cycle anyway. Worse, it attributes the message to an arbitrary module outside the
cycle (a file under `hisim/inputs/`), so a `# pylint: disable=cyclic-import` at the actual site
does nothing. It is disabled in `.prospector.yml`, matching `pylintrc-critical-only`, which
already disables it.

If the check is ever wanted back, the honest fix is to move `for_building` into the building
package and leave `SizingContext` fact-agnostic.

Done when: either the check is back with the move done, or the disable carries a note saying this
is the reason and the fix.

title: Settle the five open questions of the HPC harness spec
description:
Source: hpc_harnes_spec.md section 17, "Open questions / future"

* Autoscaler: whole-node autoscaling and proactively cancelling running (not just Slurm-PENDING)
  surplus workers are the natural follow-ups.
* Priorities and fairness across multiple submitted batches -- the schema supports `priority` and
  `batch_id`; the policy is TBD.
* Richer output validation -- section 4.8 requires a single success file for `done`; a future
  extension could let a runner check multiple files, sizes or content hashes before the rename.
* Multiple runners per server -- the database is already runner-tagged; confirm whether one
  server should host mixed-runner queues or one runner per server instance.
* Database growth at very large scale -- a `worker_metrics` downsampling policy, and possibly
  moving long-term metrics to a separate rollup database.

Also relevant to the harness, from the declarative plan's P5: the payload becomes an
energy-system string plus simulation parameters and the worker loads from the string, which
changes what a job record has to carry.

title: Check autodoc member visibility for the building package when the Sphinx docs are next built
description:
Source: roadmap/json_development/building_cleanup_findings.md, item 15

`docs/api/hisim.components.building.rst` uses `automodule` on the package, and the classes are
now imported names in `__init__` (listed in `__all__`). The docs build is not a CI gate, so this
was left unchanged -- worth a look whenever the Sphinx docs are next built, because `automodule`
on a package whose classes are re-exports can silently document nothing.

title: Explain the sporadic errors of test_building_information_for_every_tabula_code
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction]
`test_building_information_for_every_tabula_code` errors sporadically when anything else runs in
the repo concurrently"

Three `pytest -m base` runs that overlapped with other work in the same checkout (a scenario-JSON
regeneration, a parallel pytest invocation, live source edits) each produced one or two
collection/setup ERRORs on random TABULA parametrizations of this test; the identical suite run
sequentially passes twice with zero errors, and every errored parametrization passes in
isolation. Plausibly contention around a shared file (`logs/`, `results/`, or the class-scope
TABULA CSV cache being rebuilt while another process imports).

Harmless for CI, which runs one suite per checkout, but worth knowing before blaming a branch for
a red local run -- and worth a look if it ever appears in CI.

needs-triage: no owner and a named reason not to chase it. It is the same class of hazard as the
stale-cache one and the `--scan-all` non-determinism; whoever does the cache-injection work
(Rust Tier 3) should check whether it disappears.

title: Add a syntax gate to any future mechanical call-site rewriting sweep
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] Mechanical call-site
rewriting needs a syntax gate, not a diff review" and "[bug] Import-insertion tooling corrupted
one setup"

Converting the 72 `get_default_german_single_family_home` call sites with a
keyword-args-to-field-assignments script silently produced one wrecked file: the setup whose last
keyword argument ended `...,)` on the same line ran the "read until the closing paren" loop past
the end of the call and rewrote nine following statements into attribute assignments.
`compileall` over the touched trees caught it instantly.

The same shape bit once before: inserting a `SizingContext` import after
"from hisim.simulator import SimulationParameters" broke
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py`, whose import line continued with
", Simulator". Textual import insertion needs full-line anchors.

Any future sweep of this shape should run a parse gate per file, not per tree.

Done when: the rule is written where a sweep author will read it (a script helper that does the
per-file `compileall`, or a line in the repository's own conventions).

title: Keep ConfigBase annotations importable at runtime from hisim/config/base.py
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction]
`SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` needed a home on `ConfigBase`" ("third occurrence of the pattern; worth a
rule"), with the two earlier occurrences in the same document

The pattern, hit three times from three directions: a name that is not importable at runtime from
`hisim/config/base.py` must not appear in a `ConfigBase` annotation, because `dataclasses_json`
evaluates those annotations from every subclass's module.

The three occurrences: `Sizable = Union[T, _AutoSize, "SizingLaw"]` as a string forward reference
above the class made `get_type_hints` fail with `NameError` in every config module that did not
itself import `SizingLaw`, fixed by defining the alias below the class with a real reference;
`SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` had to be declared on `ConfigBase` for mypy, with its element type kept as
`Any`, because naming `FactContribution` would either invert the package layering or leave a
`TYPE_CHECKING`-only forward reference; and the general lesson for shared aliases.

Done when: the rule is stated where a config author will read it -- the `hisim/config/` package
docstring is the natural place, since it is where the layering rule already lives.

title: Review the wood-fuel emission factors against one stated accounting
description: From the PR #794 review (owner decision 2026-09-24: a bead, not in #794). With the corrected wood-chip heating value (4333.3 kWh/t, hisim-l07.15) the shipped wood-chip CO2 factors disagree per tonne: the legacy DE 2018-2024 series 0.0313 kg/kWh (src_opex_14/15, kept as published by #791) is 136 kg/t, the AI-placeholder DE/IE 2026/2035 rows derive from 80 kg/t (0.0185 kg/kWh), AT 2025/2040 is 82 kg/t. Decide one accounting (biogenic counted or not, GEG vs UBA vs legacy source), then re-derive the wood-fuel factors (pellets too) and replace the AI placeholders.

title: Stop the heat pump's space-heating controller from staying off below a low flow setpoint
description:
Found 2026-09-23 while computing comfort grades (hisim-sska) on the RenoVisor mockup package, full year 2019, IE: air/water hplib + floor heating + insulation.

MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSpaceHeating (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:2658-2686) switches on only when the buffer water is below set_heating_flow_temperature - lower_temperature_offset_for_state_conditions_in_celsius (5.0) and off above flow + upper offset (5.0). With floor heating in mild weather the HeatDistributionController asks for a flow of ~23.4 C, so the switch-on point is ~18.4 C; the buffer sits at room temperature (~18.6 C) and never gets there. The pump stays off while the distribution is on and the room sits at 18.6-19.5 C against a 21 C setpoint.

Evidence: June-August 4516 quarter-hours with room < 20.5 C, of which 4223 with SH controller off, HDS state on, window closed. 1944 of the year's 2503 K*h below setpoint fall in June-September at outdoor > 10 C. Heat delivered 26 233 kWh vs 29 425 kWh theoretical demand (-11%). The gas-boiler baseline of the same house: 331 K*h.

Consequence: every heat-pump plan with a low flow setpoint under-delivers heat, so its electricity, bills, CO2 and LCOH are too low -- the economics comparison favours the heat pump by roughly that much. Owner interview on the fix pending.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/heat-pump-switch-on-floor (decided with Noah 2026-09-23: never switch on below the room setpoint, component-wide). RenoVisor mockup package, full year IE: heat delivered 26 233 -> 26 877 kWh against 29 425 -> 27 530 kWh demand (-11% -> -2.4%), K*h below 21 C 2503 -> 729 (the rest is on/off ripple: 57 K*h beyond 1 K), grid electricity 8 490 -> 8 619 kWh. HiSim's heat-pump twin (Aachen, 2021, predefined profile): 230.5 -> 228.3 K*h, 2 253 -> 2 255 kWh.

title: Compute the comfort grades and summer heat protection from the simulated year (renovisorissues #29)
description: Frontend ask: https://jugit.fz-juelich.de/iek-3/groups/urbanmodels/renovisorissues/-/work_items/29. kpis.py _comfort() publishes the contract examples as MOCKED, the same two grades for every house. Options: compute heating/cooling grades from hours below set_heating_temperature / above a stated cooling threshold, with thresholds in the spec; or decide they stay mocked so the frontend drops them. Related: hisim-4g9.14. WAITING FOR HUMAN APPROVAL.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/computed-comfort (decisions with Noah 2026-09-23): comfort.heating = degree-hours more than 1 K below the house's own setpoint (high <= 100, medium <= 500, else low); comfort.cooling and summer_heat_protection = degree-hours above 26 C (high <= 500 / medium <= 1200; 5..1 at 250/500/900/1200); full-year runs only. Mockup full year after hisim-q1rm: baseline heating high (3 K*h), heat-pump package high (57 K*h), summer high / 5 for both.

comments.text: 2026-09-23: implemented and committed on local branch feat/computed-comfort (not pushed). On the full-year mockup it graded the gas baseline heating 'medium' (331 K*h) and the heat-pump package 'low' (2503 K*h), which exposed the controller bug hisim-q1rm. title: Check the SCOP calibration's mean-outlet anchors against measured heat pump data
description:
Source: decision with Noah, 2026-09-23, while implementing hisim-4g9.15 ("go with the mean outlet
anchors, but make a bead that we need to check this against real data").

What was decided without data: when a heat pump's datasheet states both EN 14825 SCOPs (W35 and
W55), ScopCalibration scales hplib's COP by a factor that is linear in the outlet temperature
between two anchors and constant outside them. The anchors are the heat-weighted mean outlets of
the two EN 14825 rating lines (28.9 C for W35, 40.7 C for W55), and both factors are solved so the
calibrated fit rates exactly at the stated SCOPs. The alternative, anchors at the nominal 35 / 55 C,
